file_paths.description: publish with `asset: true` only: several local image, video, PDF, font, stylesheet or script files in place of `file_path`, up to 25 in one call, all into the artifact that `url` names; one approval covers the call, and the result lists each file's id and url, or why it was not uploaded. A CSV, Markdown, JSON or plain-text file, a symbolic or hard link, and a file outside the working directory each go in a call of their own with `file_path`.

from_url.description: publish with `asset: true`, in place of `file_path`: the SOURCE artifact's claude.ai URL — one the person can open.

asset_ids.description: publish with `asset: true` and `from_url` only: 1–10 distinct asset ids from the source artifact (from a `scope: "assets"` listing of it, or an upload result).

favicon.description: Deprecated; Claude omits it and uses `icon`.

icon.description: One short generic word for the artifact's browser-tab icon, such as chart, calendar, recipe, code or map: a plain signifier, never a product or brand name. Claude includes it on every page's first publish and omits it on a redeploy so the artifact keeps its icon, passing a new one only when the person asks. Ignored on an Artifact created from an Artifact type.

files.description: Supporting files to publish alongside the page, as a map {"published/path": "source/path" | {from, contentType} | {artifact, path, ver?} | null}. The key is what the HTML references. The source is a path on disk, or {from, contentType} when the type cannot be inferred from the published extension. An {artifact, path} source copies that Artifact's published file on the server: an Artifact the person can open, with its type carried over, never an HTML or XML document, and at most 4 source Artifact versions per publish. null removes that path on an update, and files left out are kept. A plain list publishes each file at its own spelling. Sources must be under the working directory or Claude's scratchpad directory. `preflight.js` at the artifact root is reserved: it runs against open pages when Claude publishes updates, and it must be a JavaScript module of at most 8 KiB whose default export is a function, or the publish is refused.

path.description: Path relative to the working directory (or to `root`, which may be a folder in your scratchpad directory); the file is served at this same path next to the page.

contentType.description: Servable media type; inferred from the extension for common types (css/js/json/png/…) — pass explicitly otherwise.

from.description: Source file path — relative to `root` (default: the working directory), or absolute under the working directory or your scratchpad directory.

contentType.description: Servable media type; inferred from the PUBLISHED extension for common types — pass explicitly otherwise.

artifact.description: Another artifact's claude.ai URL: the file is copied from ITS published files, server side — nothing is downloaded. You must be able to open that artifact.

path.description: The file's published path inside that Artifact, as a listing of its files prints it (not "index.html").

ver.description: A version of that Artifact to copy from instead of its current one — only versions you are served (its history, if you can edit it); omit for the current version.

root.description: The base directory that relative `files` sources resolve against, like a bundler root. It never changes published paths. It is relative to the working directory, or absolute within it or within Claude's scratchpad directory. It requires `files`, except on an Artifact made from a type, where a data `file_path` under it is served at its path relative to it.

pin.description: publish only: true also pins the published artifact to the person's claude.ai sidebar once it is published. Claude passes it only when the person asked for that. A failed pin never fails the publish, and the result says so.

limit.description: list only: the maximum number of artifacts to return (default 25).

scope.description: list: which listing to return. 'mine' is the default. The others are 'shared', 'all', 'types', 'files' (with `url`) and 'assets' (with `url`, continued with `after`). See **Calls**.

type_query.description: list with scope 'types' only: limits the listing to the types whose title or description match this text best, ignoring case; a type that matches less well is left out, so a narrowed listing is not the whole catalog. Claude omits it when choosing a type for a request, unless a listing made without it says more types exist than it shows.

type.description: list only: the name of a published Artifact type, as a 'types' listing shows it (case does not matter). The listing then shows the Artifacts made from that type instead of the person's gallery. Claude passes this or `type_url`, not both.

intent.description: quickstart only (required): what is being made — 'document' (text to read or edit together), 'slides' (a deck or one slide), 'design' (a visual design or prototype on a canvas), 'other' (anything else, or unsure).

design_systems.description: quickstart only: false when a design system's link is already in hand (it is then read with its own call) or one was declined. Omitted or true, the result lists the design systems (not for a document) and, for slides or a design, attaches the default one's README.

title.description: publish: the fallback title for an HTML page whose file has no <title>. It is a name, not a summary, and Claude keeps it the same across redeploys. On a `type_url` create, it is the new Artifact's name: what the person called it, or a short descriptive name. If it is left out, the Artifact is named after the type.

description.description: publish: one sentence for the subtitle on the gallery card.

label.description: A short name for this publish, at most 60 characters (e.g. "Draft to legal"). Optional. It is a few words, not a description.

overwrite_unread.description: publish with `files` or `root` to an existing artifact: published paths this call may replace or remove although you have not read or listed them in this session. Every other path the call touches must be one you read by its `path`, saw in a file listing, or published yourself, and must not have changed since — otherwise nothing is sent and the refusal names each path. Name a path here only when the user asked for it to be replaced without looking at what is there; it never excuses a path that changed after you read it.

url.description: An existing artifact's claude.ai link (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}); a chat, project or session link is not one, and `action: "list"` lists the person's artifacts. On a publish, it is the artifact to update in place, one the person owns or was given edit access to (a read of it says "writer"). Before publishing to an artifact this conversation has neither read nor published, Claude reads it (`action: "read"`) and builds on what comes back; a publish sent without that read is refused. A refusal that hands Claude the live version counts as that read: Claude merges its changes into that version and publishes the result, and never resends the refused content unchanged. Claude omits `url` for a new artifact or to redeploy a file this conversation already published. For read, delete and the other calls that take a URL, it is the artifact to act on.

type_url.description: publish: the Artifact type to create this new, private Artifact from (a link from a 'types' listing). Claude omits `url`. Any `file_path`/`files` passed become the new Artifact's own files beside the type's fixed ones. read (no `url`): the type to describe. list: the type whose Artifacts to list, or Claude names the type with `type` instead.

auto_open.description: Only with `type_url` and no `file_path`: when the new Artifact opens for the person. Claude passes "after_first_write" when it will fill the Artifact right after creating it with a files publish to its url, so the person does not first see it empty. The Artifact then opens on that first write. Otherwise Claude omits it, and the Artifact opens when created; Claude always omits it for a type whose content it writes through a connector, such as a Claude Docs document, since no publish or store write follows to open it.

prompt.description: read, for an artifact shared with the person: what Claude needs from it, which steers the isolated summary.

force.description: publish: a last-resort overwrite that **discards** the newer published version. On a conflict, Claude merges its changes onto the newer content that the rejection hands it and publishes again. Claude passes true only when the person explicitly said to discard that specific version, and the server may still refuse it over a version saved from inside the page.

out_dir.description: read with `path`: the directory to save into. The default is this artifact's folder in Claude's scratchpad directory, where saving needs no approval. A published file lands at <out_dir>/<published path>, and saving it outside that default folder asks the person first. An asset's file is named by its id plus its type's extension; saving it outside the default folder is an ordinary file save the person may be asked to approve.

path.description: read: the file's published path inside the artifact, exactly as a 'files' listing printed it ("index.html" is the page itself). The file is saved locally, the result says where, and a small text file's contents are included. It can instead be an uploaded asset's id (32 hex characters, from an 'assets' listing or an upload result), and that asset is saved to a local file. delete: the id of the one asset to remove.

paths.description: read: several published paths in place of `path`, up to 256 in one call. Each file is saved as a single `path` would be, and the result lists where each one landed, or why it could not be read, with small text files' contents included while they fit.

after.description: list with scope 'assets' only: the `next` value from a previous listing, passed to continue it.

page.description: read only: true returns the rendered page in cases where a read otherwise returns something else. A typed Artifact's read leaves out the type's own page.

capabilities.description: publish: the runtime capabilities this page declares, as {name: config}. Claude loads the `artifact-capabilities` skill before passing it. On a redeploy Claude omits the field to keep what the page has, and {} clears it.

contract.description: publish: the artifact's runtime version. Leaving it out keeps the current version (the default), 'latest' upgrades, and an exact version pins or rolls back. It changes how the published page behaves, so Claude passes it only when the author explicitly intends that change.

tools.name: AskUserQuestion
tools.description:
Use this tool only when you are blocked on a decision that is genuinely the user's to make: one you cannot resolve from the request, the code, or sensible defaults.

Usage notes:
- Users will always be able to select "Other" to provide custom text input
- Use multiSelect: true to allow multiple answers to be selected for a question
- If you recommend a specific option, make that the first option in the list and add "(Recommended)" at the end of the label

Plan mode note: To switch into plan mode, use EnterPlanMode (not this tool). Once in plan mode, use this tool to clarify requirements or choose between approaches BEFORE finalizing your plan. Do NOT use this tool to ask "Is my plan ready?", "Should I proceed?", or otherwise reference "the plan" in questions — the user cannot see the plan until you call ExitPlanMode for approval.

Reserve this for decisions where the user's answer changes what you do next — not for choices with a conventional default or facts you can verify in the codebase yourself. In those cases pick the obvious option, mention it in your response, and proceed.

Preview feature:
Use the optional `preview` field on options when presenting concrete artifacts that users need to visually compare:
- ASCII mockups of UI layouts or components
- Code snippets showing different implementations
- Diagram variations
- Configuration examples

Preview content is rendered as markdown in a monospace box. Multi-line text with newlines is supported. When any option has a preview, the UI switches to a side-by-side layout with a vertical option list on the left and preview on the right. Do not use previews for simple preference questions where labels and descriptions suffice. Note: previews are only supported for single-select questions (not multiSelect).

questions.description: Questions to ask the user (1-4 questions)

question.description: The complete question to ask the user. Should be clear, specific, and end with a question mark. Example: "Which library should we use for date formatting?" If multiSelect is true, phrase it accordingly, e.g. "Which features do you want to enable?"

header.description: Very short label displayed as a chip/tag (max 12 chars). Examples: "Auth method", "Library", "Approach".

options.description: The available choices for this question. Must have 2-4 options. Each option should be a distinct, mutually exclusive choice (unless multiSelect is enabled). There should be no 'Other' option, that will be provided automatically.

label.description: The display text for this option that the user will see and select. Should be concise (1-5 words) and clearly describe the choice.

description.description: Explanation of what this option means or what will happen if chosen. Useful for providing context about trade-offs or implications.

preview.description: Optional preview content rendered when this option is focused. Use for mockups, code snippets, or visual comparisons that help users compare options. See the tool description for the expected content format.

multiSelect.description: Set to true to allow the user to select multiple options instead of just one. Use when choices are not mutually exclusive.

answers.description: User answers collected by the permission component

annotations.description: Optional per-question annotations from the user (e.g., notes on preview selections). Keyed by question text.

preview.description: The preview content of the selected option, if the question used previews.

notes.description: Free-text notes the user added to their selection.

metadata.description: Optional metadata for tracking and analytics purposes. Not displayed to user.

source.description: Optional identifier for the source of this question (e.g., "remember" for /remember command). Used for analytics tracking.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background.

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

tools.name: ListAgents

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

content.content:
# PLAN - how three people get the best agent running by Sunday 12:00

Status: **proposed Sat 15:10 by Jonathan (with Claude Code), not yet agreed by the team.** Owners
are open: claim a workstream in `docs/STATUS.md`. Change this file when the team changes the plan,
and log the change as a `[decision]`.

## 1. Where the points are

The final ranks the mean score per case, on hidden cases with suppliers we have not met. So the
agent must be good on average and must never throw a case away. Points come from three places:

1. **Structure of the deal - arithmetic, no persuasion needed.** Cover the whole horizon, start the
   new price late, pick the cheap payment term, Incoterm, ppm and chargeback, keep the must-haves.
   Evidence: sandbox D01 went from 0.20 to 0.79 only because the LLM agent asked for 24 months
   instead of 12 and a later start. On P01 the start date is worth more than two euros of price.
2. **Price close to what the supplier would really accept.** That needs a target per case (its
   cost, its margin, how far it moved in the past) and enough rounds used well. On D01 the agent
   accepted after 4 of 10 rounds and left 8,580 on the table.
3. **Not losing the supplier.** Tone, a real trade for every ask, arguments whose figures check
   out, and for strategic suppliers a price that leaves them a sustainable margin.

Everything in 1 is code and transfers to any hidden case. Most teams will leave it to the LLM.
We do it in code first.

## 2. The agent we build

Four parts with fixed interfaces, so three people can build in parallel without editing the same
files. Proposed location: a new package `sellm/` next to `arena_kit/` (the kit stays untouched
except for registering our agent in `cli.py`; add `sellm` to the wheel packages in `pyproject.toml`).

| Part | Does | Interface |
|---|---|---|
| **Calculator** `sellm/calc.py` | For a case and a standing offer: enumerate term sheets over `term_options`, price each with `total_cost`, say what each lever is worth to us, guard must-haves and coverage, set a target and a walk-away value, estimate the supplier's margin for the relationship term | `plan(case, threads, dossier) -> {sheets ranked by C, lever values, target, floor estimate, walk_away}` |
| **Intel** `sellm/intel.py`, `sellm/claims.py` | Built once for **all 46 detailed suppliers**, cached as files: who they are (family firm, group, job shop, monopolist), cash position, capacity, quality record, how past negotiations ended, what their notes and letters say they care about. Plus an argument bank per supplier and part with figures computed in code and checked against `facts.json` | `dossier(supplier_id, part_ids) -> text + fields`; `arguments(case, supplier_id) -> [{sentence, ids}]` |
| **Negotiator** `sellm/agent.py` | The round plan and the e-mail. Code decides the term sheets and which arguments are allowed; the LLM chooses among them and writes. Falls back to the calculator's move, never to the naive agent | `decide(case, threads) -> {supplier_id, message}` |
| **Runner and measurement** `sellm/runner.py`, `scripts/pull-runs` | All threads of an RFQ in parallel, a round budget from the time left in the wave, logs to a file, resumes after a crash. Saves every session of the team (transcript, trace, breakdown) to `runs/` so nobody replays a case to see what happened | `uv run arena run ... --agent sellm` |

## 3. Workstreams (one per person, each with its own agent sessions)

**A - Numbers and strategy** (calculator + negotiator). First deliverable: `plan()` reproduces the
P01 and D01 tables in `docs/LEARNINGS.md` and proposes the first two term sheets for every hosted
case. Then the round policy: open with a question and two or three sheets that probe what the
supplier values, trade one lever per round, never accept before the target unless the status is
`final_offer`, close on the best standing sheet when time or rounds run out.

**B - Data and arguments** (intel + claims). First deliverable: dossiers for the 22 practice
suppliers, checked by hand against two replays; then all 46. The 24 detailed suppliers that appear
in no practice case have about four documents each and are the likely pool for the hidden cases.
`negotiation_history` carries notes such as "accepted below full cost to keep the volume"
(Brandlhuber, the P01 part). Sunday 08:00: rebuild with the new release, it must be one command.

**C - Arena, measurement, final** (runner + runs + submission). First deliverable: the baseline
below and `scripts/pull-runs`. Then: RFQ threads in parallel, the 8-minute budget, the final
machine, the rehearsal, the README run instructions, the approach text and the slides.

Integration points: A needs B's dossier format by Sat 17:00 (agree the fields first, fill them
later). C runs every new agent version and reports per case what the cost breakdown says we lost.

## 4. Timeline (CEST)

| When | Milestone |
|---|---|
| Sat 15:30 | **Baseline** (done, see `runs/README.md`): kit LLM agent on all 10 hosted cases and on D02. We then know `C_open` and `C_best` of every case and can score any term sheet offline |
| Sat 17:00 | Interfaces agreed; `runs/` in the repo; lever table for all 10 cases |
| Sat 19:00 | Each part works alone: calculator offline, dossiers for the practice suppliers, runner on `arena-sim` |
| Sat 20:30 | Agent v1 integrated, plays D01 and D02 without errors; **full practice run 1** |
| Sat 23:00 | v2 after reading the replays; **full practice run 2**. Slides skeleton. Then sleep |
| Sun 08:00 | Data release: `uv run arena data`, rebuild dossiers, one sanity run |
| Sun 09:00 | Pre-flight on the final machine and network |
| Sun 10:00 | **Rehearsal**: all 10 hosted cases in parallel, every case done inside 6.5 minutes |
| Sun 11:00 | Our own freeze: no behaviour changes after this. README, approach text, slides, commit hash |
| Sun 11:30 | Runner started and logging; checklist in `docs/CONTEXT.md` section 12 |
| Sun 12:00 | Live Final |

## 5. Quota budget (199 sessions left, no refill before the final)

| Use | Sessions |
|---|---|
| Baseline now | 10 |
| Full runs of a new agent version (run 1, run 2, one spare) | 30 |
| Single-case experiments, each testing one stated hypothesis | 80 |
| Sunday: sanity run after the data release, pre-flight, rehearsal | 25 |
| Reserve | 54 |

Rules: `AGENTS.md` section 5. Every run is logged with the quota left. A practice session without
a hypothesis written down first is a wasted session.

## 6. How we test

1. **Offline first.** With `C_open` and `C_best` known, `total_cost` gives the score of any term
   sheet for free. Most of part 1 above is tested this way.
2. **Sandbox for behaviour** (free, real supplier bots): Does pushing on after `agreed` work or
   backfire? How many rounds until `final_offer`? Does an RFQ thread time out while we wait on
   another? What does a cost-breakdown request return? Which opening gets the largest first move?
3. **Practice to confirm**, one case at a time, then a full run per agent version.
4. **Read the trace, not the back office.** `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}` has the supplier's reasons per
   move. The back office only shows who asked whom ("My call: counter.") and is not worth parsing.

## 7. Risks

- **Time in the final.** A round takes about 30 s including the supplier's reply; a wave gives
  about 6.5 usable minutes. Ten rounds do not fit, and an RFQ with three suppliers handled one after
  another fits even less. The runner needs parallel threads and a round budget.
- **Overfitting.** Up to a third of the hidden cases combine supplier and case types practice never
  shows. No rule may mention a practice case or supplier by name; everything is driven by the case
  file, the dossier and the calculator.
- **Silent LLM failure.** Today a failed call plays the naive move. Our fallback must be the
  calculator's best move, and the runner must log every fallback.
- **A wrong figure costs trust.** Arguments come from the argument bank only; the LLM may not
  write a number or an ID that code did not give it.
- **One machine, one key.** Decide the final machine today (open question in `docs/STATUS.md`).

## 8. Data access, timing and overfitting (decided Sat 15:20)

**No vector database, no embeddings.** The data is small and keyed by ID: all 208 letters, e-mails
and notes together are 46 KB; everything written about one supplier is at most about 500 tokens;
reading it by `supplier_id` takes 0.1 ms. Similarity search would add a dependency, latency and
wrong hits and solve a problem we do not have. Instead:

- **Dossier cache**: one command builds a file per supplier (and per part) from SQL plus the full
  text of its documents, with an LLM summary written offline. Runtime is a dictionary lookup by the
  case's `suppliers` and `parts`. Sunday 08:00: `uv run arena data`, run the command again, commit.
- **Optimal values are computed, never retrieved.** The best term sheet depends on the case's
  rates, options and must-haves, which are new in every hidden case. The calculator derives it from
  the case file in milliseconds. Storing "what worked on P01" and looking it up is overfitting.
- **A supplier with no dossier must still work**: hidden cases carry `facts` that exist only in
  the case file. The agent builds a minimal dossier from those at the start of the case.

**Where the time goes.** The 60-second clock starts when the session opens and runs per thread.
Case files are readable before that (`GET /v1/cases?set=final` once the wave has started), so all
preparation happens **before** `POST /v1/sessions`: dossier lookup, plan, argument bank, and one
planning call to the LLM if we want one. Inside the session a move is the calculator (milliseconds)
plus one LLM call for the wording. Budget: 15 s per move as the target, 40 s as the hard deadline
after which the calculator's move is sent without the LLM. Nothing in a move may search or summarise.

**Guards against overfitting** (the hidden set includes combinations practice never hosts):

- No practice case ID, supplier ID or supplier name anywhere in code or prompts. Review for it.
- The calculator must handle **every** negotiable field. `incoterm` is negotiable in no practice
  case, `tooling_eur` in one, `effective_date` in two; the final may use any of them.
- Dry-run the whole pipeline (prepare, plan, first message) on all 19 practice case files, not only
  the 10 hosted ones. `P06` (rfq + stabilise) and `P13` (price_increase + leverage) are
  combinations that are never hosted, which is what the final will look like.
- Property tests on generated case files: random negotiable sets, options, must-haves and goals.
  Every proposed sheet has exactly the negotiable fields, values from `term_options`, keeps the
  must-haves and has a finite C.
- Hold out 3 of the 10 hosted cases (P04, P10, P18): never look at them while tuning, play them
  only in full runs. If the held-out mean falls behind the others, we are overfitting.
- Judge a change by the mean over cases, never by one case.

## 9. Not doing

- No vector database or embedding search (section 8).
- No supplier simulator of our own: too much work for what it would prove before Sunday.
- No tuning on a single practice case until it scores 1.0: the final cases are different ones.
- No changes to `arena_kit/` beyond registering our agent, so upstream fixes stay easy to take.
# LEARNINGS - what works and what fails in negotiations

Durable findings with their evidence. Add one when a replay, a cost breakdown or an offline
calculation teaches something that should change how the agent behaves. State how sure we are:
**confirmed** (seen in our own replay), **computed** (from the cost function), **reported** (from
Tacto's docs or FAQ, not yet seen by us). Raw history goes to `docs/LOG.md`.

## General

- **Tone and relationship move price** (reported, FAQ P01 recording). Appreciation for past
  fairness plus one verified index plus an offer to pay faster got 0.76. The same index sent as an
  ultimatum got EUR 136.50 from November instead of January, about EUR 13,700 a year worse.
- **Price is only one lever, and often not the biggest** (computed, P01 below). The kit's naive
  agent negotiates price only and leaves the other fields at the supplier's opening values.
- **The kit agents ignore the relationship term** (confirmed in code). In `stabilise` and
  `secure_supply` cases the arena charges for leaving the supplier below its sustainable margin;
  `total_cost` only includes it when given a supplier estimate. Our P01 deal at EUR 135.40 showed
  `relationship: 0.0` in the arena's breakdown, so that price did not squeeze Brandlhuber.
- **Answer "which figures?" with data** (reported, FAQ P01 recording). The supplier asked for the
  basis of our price; citing the should-cost estimate (`cost:310010`) was `verified` and brought
  the closing offer.

## From the baseline of all 10 hosted cases (Sat 15:27, kit LLM agent, mean 61.5)

Full analysis with evidence per case: `runs/BASELINE.md`. The rules that follow from it:

- **Price every sheet a supplier sends and compare by C** (seen, computed). Suppliers put two
  packages in one e-mail in 11 of 12 threads; the kit reads only the first. In P10 the ignored
  alternative was worth 0.647 against the accepted 0.570.
- **Do not stop when the supplier stops moving** (seen). The kit agent accepted after 2-5 of 10
  messages, on the first `final_offer`, `agreed` or repeated price. What happens when we answer a
  final offer with a different package is not tested yet.
- **Talk to all RFQ threads in parallel** (seen, P05): handled one by one, the waiting threads
  timed out and the cheapest bidder withdrew.
- **Never cite the same ID twice in a case** (seen): 8 of 16 claims came back `duplicate`. Bring a
  new, checked figure each round, and have data ready when the supplier asks "Which figures is
  that based on?" (P03, P04, P05, P10).
- **Should-cost is the price target** (computed): where an estimate for the supplier's own plant

# PLAN - how three people get the best agent running by Sunday 12:00

Status: **proposed Sat 15:10 by Jonathan (with Claude Code), not yet agreed by the team.** Owners
are open: claim a workstream in `docs/STATUS.md`. Change this file when the team changes the plan,
and log the change as a `[decision]`.

## 1. Where the points are

The final ranks the mean score per case, on hidden cases with suppliers we have not met. So the
agent must be good on average and must never throw a case away. Points come from three places:

1. **Structure of the deal - arithmetic, no persuasion needed.** Cover the whole horizon, start the
   new price late, pick the cheap payment term, Incoterm, ppm and chargeback, keep the must-haves.
   Evidence: sandbox D01 went from 0.20 to 0.79 only because the LLM agent asked for 24 months
   instead of 12 and a later start. On P01 the start date is worth more than two euros of price.
2. **Price close to what the supplier would really accept.** That needs a target per case (its
   cost, its margin, how far it moved in the past) and enough rounds used well. On D01 the agent
   accepted after 4 of 10 rounds and left 8,580 on the table.
3. **Not losing the supplier.** Tone, a real trade for every ask, arguments whose figures check
   out, and for strategic suppliers a price that leaves them a sustainable margin.

Everything in 1 is code and transfers to any hidden case. Most teams will leave it to the LLM.
We do it in code first.

## 2. The agent we build

Four parts with fixed interfaces, so three people can build in parallel without editing the same
files. Proposed location: a new package `sellm/` next to `arena_kit/` (the kit stays untouched
except for registering our agent in `cli.py`; add `sellm` to the wheel packages in `pyproject.toml`).

| Part | Does | Interface |
|---|---|---|
| **Calculator** `sellm/calc.py` | For a case and a standing offer: enumerate term sheets over `term_options`, price each with `total_cost`, say what each lever is worth to us, guard must-haves and coverage, set a target and a walk-away value, estimate the supplier's margin for the relationship term | `plan(case, threads, dossier) -> {sheets ranked by C, lever values, target, floor estimate, walk_away}` |
| **Intel** `sellm/intel.py`, `sellm/claims.py` | Built once for **all 46 detailed suppliers**, cached as files: who they are (family firm, group, job shop, monopolist), cash position, capacity, quality record, how past negotiations ended, what their notes and letters say they care about. Plus an argument bank per supplier and part with figures computed in code and checked against `facts.json` | `dossier(supplier_id, part_ids) -> text + fields`; `arguments(case, supplier_id) -> [{sentence, ids}]` |
| **Negotiator** `sellm/agent.py` | The round plan and the e-mail. Code decides the term sheets and which arguments are allowed; the LLM chooses among them and writes. Falls back to the calculator's move, never to the naive agent | `decide(case, threads) -> {supplier_id, message}` |
| **Runner and measurement** `sellm/runner.py`, `scripts/pull-runs` | All threads of an RFQ in parallel, a round budget from the time left in the wave, logs to a file, resumes after a crash. Saves every session of the team (transcript, trace, breakdown) to `runs/` so nobody replays a case to see what happened | `uv run arena run ... --agent sellm` |

## 3. Workstreams (one per person, each with its own agent sessions)

**A - Numbers and strategy** (calculator + negotiator). First deliverable: `plan()` reproduces the
P01 and D01 tables in `docs/LEARNINGS.md` and proposes the first two term sheets for every hosted
case. Then the round policy: open with a question and two or three sheets that probe what the
supplier values, trade one lever per round, never accept before the target unless the status is
`final_offer`, close on the best standing sheet when time or rounds run out.

**B - Data and arguments** (intel + claims). First deliverable: dossiers for the 22 practice
suppliers, checked by hand against two replays; then all 46. The 24 detailed suppliers that appear
in no practice case have about four documents each and are the likely pool for the hidden cases.
`negotiation_history` carries notes such as "accepted below full cost to keep the volume"
(Brandlhuber, the P01 part). Sunday 08:00: rebuild with the new release, it must be one command.

**C - Arena, measurement, final** (runner + runs + submission). First deliverable: the baseline
below and `scripts/pull-runs`. Then: RFQ threads in parallel, the 8-minute budget, the final
machine, the rehearsal, the README run instructions, the approach text and the slides.

Integration points: A needs B's dossier format by Sat 17:00 (agree the fields first, fill them
later). C runs every new agent version and reports per case what the cost breakdown says we lost.

## 4. Timeline (CEST)

| When | Milestone |
|---|---|
| Sat 15:30 | **Baseline** (done, see `runs/README.md`): kit LLM agent on all 10 hosted cases and on D02. We then know `C_open` and `C_best` of every case and can score any term sheet offline |
| Sat 17:00 | Interfaces agreed; `runs/` in the repo; lever table for all 10 cases |
| Sat 19:00 | Each part works alone: calculator offline, dossiers for the practice suppliers, runner on `arena-sim` |
| Sat 20:30 | Agent v1 integrated, plays D01 and D02 without errors; **full practice run 1** |
| Sat 23:00 | v2 after reading the replays; **full practice run 2**. Slides skeleton. Then sleep |
| Sun 08:00 | Data release: `uv run arena data`, rebuild dossiers, one sanity run |
| Sun 09:00 | Pre-flight on the final machine and network |
| Sun 10:00 | **Rehearsal**: all 10 hosted cases in parallel, every case done inside 6.5 minutes |
| Sun 11:00 | Our own freeze: no behaviour changes after this. README, approach text, slides, commit hash |
| Sun 11:30 | Runner started and logging; checklist in `docs/CONTEXT.md` section 12 |
| Sun 12:00 | Live Final |

## 5. Quota budget (199 sessions left, no refill before the final)

| Use | Sessions |
|---|---|
| Baseline now | 10 |
| Full runs of a new agent version (run 1, run 2, one spare) | 30 |
| Single-case experiments, each testing one stated hypothesis | 80 |
| Sunday: sanity run after the data release, pre-flight, rehearsal | 25 |
| Reserve | 54 |

Rules: `AGENTS.md` section 5. Every run is logged with the quota left. A practice session without
a hypothesis written down first is a wasted session.

## 6. How we test

1. **Offline first.** With `C_open` and `C_best` known, `total_cost` gives the score of any term
   sheet for free. Most of part 1 above is tested this way.
2. **Sandbox for behaviour** (free, real supplier bots): Does pushing on after `agreed` work or
   backfire? How many rounds until `final_offer`? Does an RFQ thread time out while we wait on
   another? What does a cost-breakdown request return? Which opening gets the largest first move?
3. **Practice to confirm**, one case at a time, then a full run per agent version.
4. **Read the trace, not the back office.** `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}` has the supplier's reasons per
   move. The back office only shows who asked whom ("My call: counter.") and is not worth parsing.

## 7. Risks

- **Time in the final.** A round takes about 30 s including the supplier's reply; a wave gives
  about 6.5 usable minutes. Ten rounds do not fit, and an RFQ with three suppliers handled one after
  another fits even less. The runner needs parallel threads and a round budget.
- **Overfitting.** Up to a third of the hidden cases combine supplier and case types practice never
  shows. No rule may mention a practice case or supplier by name; everything is driven by the case
  file, the dossier and the calculator.
- **Silent LLM failure.** Today a failed call plays the naive move. Our fallback must be the
  calculator's best move, and the runner must log every fallback.
- **A wrong figure costs trust.** Arguments come from the argument bank only; the LLM may not
  write a number or an ID that code did not give it.
- **One machine, one key.** Decide the final machine today (open question in `docs/STATUS.md`).

## 8. Data access, timing and overfitting (decided Sat 15:20)

**No vector database, no embeddings.** The data is small and keyed by ID: all 208 letters, e-mails
and notes together are 46 KB; everything written about one supplier is at most about 500 tokens;
reading it by `supplier_id` takes 0.1 ms. Similarity search would add a dependency, latency and
wrong hits and solve a problem we do not have. Instead:

- **Dossier cache**: one command builds a file per supplier (and per part) from SQL plus the full
  text of its documents, with an LLM summary written offline. Runtime is a dictionary lookup by the
  case's `suppliers` and `parts`. Sunday 08:00: `uv run arena data`, run the command again, commit.
- **Optimal values are computed, never retrieved.** The best term sheet depends on the case's
  rates, options and must-haves, which are new in every hidden case. The calculator derives it from
  the case file in milliseconds. Storing "what worked on P01" and looking it up is overfitting.
- **A supplier with no dossier must still work**: hidden cases carry `facts` that exist only in
  the case file. The agent builds a minimal dossier from those at the start of the case.

**Where the time goes.** The 60-second clock starts when the session opens and runs per thread.
Case files are readable before that (`GET /v1/cases?set=final` once the wave has started), so all
preparation happens **before** `POST /v1/sessions`: dossier lookup, plan, argument bank, and one
planning call to the LLM if we want one. Inside the session a move is the calculator (milliseconds)
plus one LLM call for the wording. Budget: 15 s per move as the target, 40 s as the hard deadline
after which the calculator's move is sent without the LLM. Nothing in a move may search or summarise.

**Guards against overfitting** (the hidden set includes combinations practice never hosts):

- No practice case ID, supplier ID or supplier name anywhere in code or prompts. Review for it.
- The calculator must handle **every** negotiable field. `incoterm` is negotiable in no practice
  case, `tooling_eur` in one, `effective_date` in two; the final may use any of them.

- Hold out 3 of the 10 hosted cases (P04, P10, P18): never look at them while tuning, play them

- Judge a change by the mean over cases, never by one case.

- No vector database or embedding search (section 8).
- No supplier simulator of our own: too much work for what it would prove before Sunday.

# Baseline: the kit's LLM agent on all 10 hosted practice cases

Sat 2026-10-10 15:27-15:31 CEST. `uv run arena run --set practice --agent llm --parallel 10 -v`
with the kit's agent unchanged (repo at `6ba71cd`), OpenAI `gpt-6.1-sol`. Ten sessions, quota 199
-> 189. No `LLM failed`, no fallback to the naive move. Run log:
`runs/logs/2026-10-10-1527-baseline-kit-llm.log`. Every session in full: `runs/practice/<case>/`,
index in `runs/README.md`.

**Mean score 61.5.** This is the number our own agent has to beat.

## Results

"Our messages" counts negotiating e-mails before the accept; the limit is 10 per thread.

| Case | Type / goal | Score | Our messages | Supplier's last status | Deal | Gap to C_best | Mostly lost on |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| P02 | price_increase / stabilise | **0.105** | 4 | final_offer | 370.15, 30 d, no index clause | 42,371 | payment term (90 d is worth 30,155) and price |
| P18 | raw_material / leverage | **0.377** | 3 | final_offer | 5.60, index clause, 60 d, 24 m | 45,178 | price (C_best is at about 4.73) |
| P08 | raw_material / leverage | **0.433** | 5 | final_offer | 5.54, index clause, 60 d, 36 m | 99,528 | price (C_best is at about 5.10) |
| P10 | capacity / secure_supply | 0.570 | 2 | final_offer | 33.60, 23,400/y, 36 m, 42 d lead time | 259,372 | price; took the dearer of two packages |
| P05 | rfq / leverage | 0.676 | 1-4 per thread | final_offer | 29.50, 30 d, 35 d lead time (sup:70250) | 26,592 | price; timeouts on the other threads |
| P11 | quality / quality_first | 0.710 | 5 | agreed | 45.50, 300 ppm, chargeback 0 | 27,582 | price |
| P07 | bundling / routine | 0.779 | 4 | final_offer | 5.36, 90 d, 24 m | 20,243 | price |
| P01 | price_increase / stabilise | 0.789 | 5 | open (held its price twice) | 133.70, 14 d, from Jan 2027 | 11,995 | start date (April is worth 14,556) |
| P04 | renewal / routine | 0.810 | 3 | final_offer | 4.91, 60 d, 24 m | 441 | payment term (90 d is worth 1,309) |
| P03 | renewal / stabilise | 0.903 | 4 | open | 432.94, 90 d, 36 m, 4,580/y | 32,587 | price |

Score points lost, of 10 possible: 3.85. Three cases (P02, P18, P08) account for 2.09 of them.

## What the baseline shows

Each finding says how sure it is: **seen** in these sessions, **computed** offline with the cost
function, or **open** (a hypothesis).

### 1. The agent stops as soon as the supplier stops moving (seen, all cases)

It accepted on the first `final_offer` (7 cases), on `agreed` (P11) or when the supplier repeated
its price (P01, P03). It used 2 to 5 of its 10 messages; in P10 it accepted after two. It never
tests whether a final offer is final, and never brings a new trade once the supplier says "final". What a supplier does
when we answer a final offer with a different package instead of a lower price is **open**: test
it in the sandbox before building on it.

reply. Using all ten rounds would take about five to six minutes per case, close to the limit of a
final wave (6.5 usable minutes).

"""arena-sim: a minimal arena that speaks the public API exactly - to learn the contract.

Same paths, fields, statuses, errors and limits as the hosted arena; quote PDFs and cost-breakdown

--no-clock switches the 60-second rule off (threads wait forever) to try the API by hand.
"""

import argparse
import datetime
import hashlib
import html
import io
import itertools
import json
import re
import threading
import time
from pathlib import Path

from .cost import closing_terms, cost_breakdown, must_haves_ok, score, total_cost
from .docs import LABELS

CASES = Path(__file__).parent / "sim_cases"
MOVE_S, MAX_OPEN, MAX_CALLS, MAX_BODY = 60, 10, 10, 64_000
PRACTICE_LIMIT, DAY_S, REMAINING = 200, 86_400, "X-Practice-Remaining"  # the arena's practice quota
OPEN_UP, STEP, FLOOR, FINAL_ROUND = 0.10, 0.02, 0.90, 5
ID_RE = re.compile(r"\b(?:idx|quote|offer|sc|qn|po|cost|fc|news|doc|ctr):[\w.:@#/-]*\w")
LATE = "late: more than 60 s after the supplier's last move, so it counted as a timeout"
NAMES = {field: label for label, field in LABELS.items()}
SIGNALS = {"reply_delay_days": 1, "validity_days": 30}


def _fmt(v):
    return "none" if v is None else f"{v:.2f}" if isinstance(v, float) else str(v)


def pdf(title, sections):
    """A one-page PDF of text lines, labelled like the arena's quotes."""
    lines = [title]
    for head, terms in sections:
        lines += [head, *(f"{NAMES.get(k, k)} {_fmt(v)}" for k, v in terms.items())]
    esc = [x.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace("(", "\\(").replace(")", "\\)") for x in lines]
    text = "".join(f"BT /F1 10 Tf 50 {800 - 14 * i} Td ({t}) Tj ET\n" for i, t in enumerate(esc))
    page = "/MediaBox [0 0 595 842] /Resources << /Font << /F1 4 0 R >> >> /Contents 5 0 R"
    objs = [
        "<< /Type /Catalog /Pages 2 0 R >>",
        "<< /Type /Pages /Kids [3 0 R] /Count 1 >>",
        f"<< /Type /Page /Parent 2 0 R {page} >>",
        "<< /Type /Font /Subtype /Type1 /BaseFont /Helvetica >>",
        f"<< /Length {len(text)} >>\nstream\n{text}endstream",
    ]
    out, offsets = "%PDF-1.4\n", []
    for i, obj in enumerate(objs, 1):
        offsets.append(len(out))
        out += f"{i} 0 obj\n{obj}\nendobj\n"
    xref = f"xref\n0 {len(objs) + 1}\n0000000000 65535 f \n"
    xref += "".join(f"{o:010d} 00000 n \n" for o in offsets)
    tail = f"trailer\n<< /Size {len(objs) + 1} /Root 1 0 R >>\nstartxref\n{len(out)}\n%%EOF\n"
    return (out + xref + tail).encode("latin-1", "replace")


def xlsx(price):
    from openpyxl import Workbook

    wb = Workbook()
    ws = wb.active
    ws.title = "Cost breakdown"
    ws.append(["Element", "EUR per unit", "Share of price"])
    for i, (name, share) in enumerate(
        [("Material", 0.5), ("Conversion", 0.3), ("Overhead", 0.15), ("Margin", 0.05)], 2
    ):
        ws.append([name, round(price * share, 2), f"=B{i}/B6"])
    ws.append(["Unit price", "=SUM(B2:B5)", "=SUM(C2:C5)"])
    buf = io.BytesIO()
    wb.save(buf)
    return buf.getvalue()


def structured(msg, round_):
    """A supplier e-mail in the structured shape of the /moves path."""
    sheet = (msg["term_sheets"] or [{}])[0]
    return {
        "offer_id": sheet.get("term_sheet_id"),
        "round": round_,
        "status": msg["status"],
        "terms": sheet.get("terms", {}),
        "missing_fields": msg["missing_fields"],
        "claims": [],
        "claim_results": msg["claim_results"],
        "signals": SIGNALS,
        "text": msg["body"],
    }


class Fail(Exception):
    def __init__(self, status, detail, headers=None):
        self.status, self.detail, self.headers = status, detail, headers


class Sim:
    """The arena's state and its one scripted supplier. One lock serialises every call."""

    def __init__(self, cases, facts=None, event_code="sim", clock=time.time, no_clock=False):
        self.cases, self.facts, self.code, self.clock = cases, facts or {}, event_code, clock
        self.no_clock = no_clock  # no 60-second rule: to try the API by hand
        self.teams, self.sessions, self.replies, self.calls = {}, {}, {}, {}
        self.ids, self.lock = itertools.count(1), threading.Lock()

    # -- the scripted supplier -----------------------------------------------------------------
    def _mail(self, s, th, status, stated, text, files=()):
        th["n"] += 1
        th.update(status=status, stated=stated, offer_id=f"offer:{th['key']}-{th['round']}")
        s["offers"][th["offer_id"]] = stated
        sheets = [] if status == "walked_away" else [{"term_sheet_id": th["offer_id"], "terms": stated}]
        msg = {
            "thread_id": f"thread:{s['case']['case_id'][5:]}:{th['key']}",
            "message_id": f"msg:{th['key']}-{th['round']}-{th['n']}",
            "in_reply_to": None,
            "from": f"sales@{th['key']}",
            "subject": f"Re: {s['case']['title']}",
            "body": f"Simulated supplier. {text}",
            "refs": [],
            "action": None,
            "term_sheets": sheets,
            "status": status,
            "signals": SIGNALS,
            "claim_results": [],
            "missing_fields": sorted(set(s["case"]["negotiable"]) - set(stated)),
            "attachments": [],
        }
        for kind in files:
            att = f"att:{th['key']}-{th['round']}-{kind.split('.')[0]}"
            s["files"][att] = (kind, dict(stated), dict(th["standard"]))
            msg["attachments"].append(
                {"attachment_id": att, "name": kind, "type": kind[-4:].strip("."), "content_b64": None}
            )
        th["messages"].append(msg)
        return msg

    def _answer(self, s, th, msg, sheets):
        results = []
        for i, ref in enumerate(list(dict.fromkeys(msg.get("refs", []) + ID_RE.findall(msg.get("body", ""))))[:3]):
            known = ref in self.facts or ref in s["case"].get("facts", {}) or ref in s["offers"]
            # a rival's quote may be cited to every bidder: it counts once per supplier, the rest once per case
            seen = (th["key"], ref) if ref.startswith(("quote:", "offer:")) else ref
            result = "contradicted" if not known else "duplicate" if seen in s["used"] else "verified"
            results.append({"index": i, "result": result})
            if known:
                s["used"].add(seen)
        files = ["cost-breakdown.xlsx"] if "breakdown" in msg.get("body", "").lower() else []
        price = round(max(th["opening"] * FLOOR, th["stated"]["unit_price"] - th["opening"] * STEP), 2)
        best = max(sheets, key=lambda t: t["unit_price"]) if sheets else None
        if best is None:
            reply = self._mail(s, th, th["status"], th["stated"], "We keep our offer.", files)
        elif best["unit_price"] >= price:
            reply = self._mail(s, th, "agreed", best, "We agree.", [*files, "quote.pdf"])
        elif th["status"] == "final_offer":
            th["closed"] = "walked_away"
            reply = self._mail(s, th, "walked_away", th["stated"], "We end here.")
        elif th["round"] >= FINAL_ROUND:
            reply = self._mail(s, th, "final_offer", {"unit_price": price}, "Final offer.", [*files, "quote.pdf"])
        else:
            reply = self._mail(s, th, "open", {"unit_price": price}, "Our counter-offer.", files)
        reply["claim_results"] = results
        s["trace"].append(
            {
                "round": th["round"],
                "actor": f"sup:{th['key']}",
                "move": structured(reply, th["round"]),
                "reasons": ["A fixed script: it concedes the same step per term sheet, down to its floor."],
            }  # the practice shape: the move and the supplier's reasons in words
        )
        return reply

    def _check(self, case, terms, th):
        if set(terms) != set(case["negotiable"]) or not (terms.get("unit_price") or 0) > 0:
            raise Fail(422, f"a term sheet carries exactly the negotiable fields {case['negotiable']}")
        for f, v in terms.items():
            options = case["term_options"].get(f)
            if f != "unit_price" and options and v not in options and v != th["standard"].get(f):
                raise Fail(422, f"{f}={v!r} is not one of {options}")
        return terms

    # -- sessions ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def open(self, team, case_id):
        case = self.cases.get(case_id)
        if case is None:
            raise Fail(404, "no such case")
        if sum(s["status"] == "open" for s in self._mine(team)) >= MAX_OPEN:
            raise Fail(429, f"at most {MAX_OPEN} open sessions per key")
        if (p := self.practice(team))["left"] == 0:  # no Retry-After: retrying does not help
            raise Fail(429, f"practice limit: {PRACTICE_LIMIT} sessions per team in 24 hours; resets_at "
                       f"{p['resets_at']}", {REMAINING: "0"})  # fmt: skip
        sid, current = f"sim{next(self.ids)}", case["buyer"].get("current_unit_price")
        s = {
            "id": sid,
            "team": team,
            "case": case,
            "status": "open",
            "end_reason": None,
            "threads": {},
            "files": {},
            "offers": {},
            "used": set(),
            "result": None,
            "trace": [],
            "moves": [],
            "created_at": self.clock(),
            "late": set(),
        }
        for i, sup in enumerate(case["suppliers"]):
            opening = round((current or case["buyer"]["fallback_unit_price"]) * (1 + OPEN_UP + 0.02 * i), 2)
            standard = {f: (case["term_options"].get(f) or [None])[0] for f in case["negotiable"][1:]}
            th = s["threads"][sup] = {
                "key": sup.split(":", 1)[1],
                "round": 0,
                "n": 0,
                "timeouts": 0,
                "closed": None,
                "last_at": self.clock(),
                "messages": [],
                "late": [],
                "standard": standard,
                "opening": opening,
            }
            self._mail(s, th, "open", {"unit_price": opening}, "Our quote is attached.", ["quote.pdf"])
        self.sessions[sid] = s
        return {
            "session_id": sid,
            "case": case,
            "opening": {k: structured(th["messages"][0], 0) for k, th in s["threads"].items()},
            "threads": {k: list(th["messages"]) for k, th in s["threads"].items()},
        }

    def _mine(self, team):
        return [s for s in self.sessions.values() if s["team"] == team]

    def practice(self, team):
        """The team's practice quota in the rolling 24 hours, as GET /v1/me shows it."""
        day = sorted(s["created_at"] for s in self._mine(team) if s["created_at"] > self.clock() - DAY_S)
        frees = datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp(day[0] + DAY_S, datetime.UTC).isoformat() if day else None
        return {
            "used": len(day),
            "left": max(0, PRACTICE_LIMIT - len(day)),
            "limit": PRACTICE_LIMIT,
            "resets_at": frees,
        }

    def session(self, team, sid):
        s = self.sessions.get(sid)
        if s is None or s["team"] != team:
            raise Fail(404, "no such session")
        s["late"] = self._tick(s)
        return s

    def _tick(self, s):
        """The 60-second rule: a supplier left waiting counts a timeout - its offer stands; the
        third in a row (or one after the last round) ends the thread. Returns who just got one."""
        late = set()
        if self.no_clock:
            return late
        for sup, th in s["threads"].items():
            while s["status"] == "open" and not th["closed"] and self.clock() > th["last_at"] + MOVE_S:
                th["last_at"] += MOVE_S
                th["round"] += 1
                th["timeouts"] += 1
                th["late"].append({"offer_id": th["offer_id"], "status": th["status"], "terms": th["stated"]})
                if th["timeouts"] >= 3 or th["round"] >= s["case"]["round_limit"]:
                    th["closed"] = "timeout"
                late.add(sup)
        self._settle(s, "timeout")
        return late

    def _settle(self, s, reason):
        if s["status"] == "open" and all(th["closed"] for th in s["threads"].values()):
            self._end(s, reason, None)

    def _end(self, s, reason, sup):
        case, ths = s["case"], s["threads"]
        c_open = min(total_cost(case, {"unit_price": th["opening"]}, th["standard"]) for th in ths.values())
        # the best this script would ever accept: its floor price, any allowed values of the other terms
        options = [case["term_options"].get(f) or [None] for f in case["negotiable"][1:]]
        c_best = min(
            total_cost(
                case,
                {
                    **dict(zip(case["negotiable"][1:], combo, strict=True)),
                    "unit_price": round(th["opening"] * FLOOR, 2),
                },
            )
            for th in ths.values()
            for combo in itertools.product(*options)
        )
        alt = case["buyer"].get("alternative") or {}
        c_alt = total_cost(case, alt["terms"]) if alt.get("terms", {}).get("unit_price") else None
        r = {
            "ended": True,
            "deal": False,
            "supplier_id": None,
            "offer_id": None,
            "terms": None,
            "c_open": c_open,
            "c_deal": None,
            "c_alt": c_alt,
            "c_best": c_best,
            "score": score(c_open, c_alt, c_best) if c_alt else 0.0,
            "must_haves_ok": None,
            "cost_breakdown": None,
            "trace": [],
        }
        if sup:
            t = closing_terms(case, ths[sup]["stated"], ths[sup]["standard"])
            r.update(
                deal=True,
                supplier_id=sup,
                offer_id=ths[sup]["offer_id"],
                terms=t,
                c_deal=total_cost(case, t),
                must_haves_ok=must_haves_ok(case, t),
                cost_breakdown=cost_breakdown(case, t),
            )
            r["score"] = score(c_open, r["c_deal"], c_best) if r["must_haves_ok"] else 0.0
        s.update(status="ended", end_reason=reason, result=r)
        for th in ths.values():
            th["closed"] = th["closed"] or reason

    def message(self, team, sid, sup, msg):
        s = self.session(team, sid)
        if s["status"] != "open":
            raise Fail(409, f"the session has ended: {s['end_reason']}")
        if sup not in s["threads"]:
            raise Fail(422, f"{sup} is not a supplier in this case")
        th, action = s["threads"][sup], msg.get("action") or {}
        if action.get("type") == "walk_away":
            self._end(s, "walked_away", None)
            note = {"body": "Simulated supplier. Understood - no deal.", "term_sheets": [], "attachments": []}
            return {**th["messages"][-1], **note, "result": _public(s["result"])}
        if sup in s["late"]:
            raise Fail(409, f"{LATE}; GET the thread for the supplier's answer")
        if th["closed"]:
            raise Fail(409, f"the thread with {sup} has ended: {th['closed']}")
        if action.get("type") == "accept":
            sheet = action.get("term_sheet_id")
            owner = next((k for k, t in s["threads"].items() if t["offer_id"] == sheet and not t["closed"]), None)
            if owner is None:
                raise Fail(422, "not a standing offer in this session")
            reply = self._mail(
                s,
                s["threads"][owner],
                "agreed",
                s["threads"][owner]["stated"],
                "Thank you for your order.",
                ["order-confirmation.pdf"],
            )
            self._end(s, "accepted", owner)
            return {**reply, "result": _public(s["result"])}
        if action:
            raise Fail(422, "action is {'type': 'accept', 'term_sheet_id': ...} or 'walk_away'")
        sheets = [self._check(s["case"], ts.get("terms", {}), th) for ts in msg.get("term_sheets") or []]
        if len(sheets) > 3 or len(msg.get("body", "")) > 8000 or len(msg.get("refs", [])) > 20:
            raise Fail(422, "at most 3 term sheets, 8,000 characters and 20 refs")
        if th["round"] >= s["case"]["round_limit"]:
            raise Fail(409, "round limit reached: accept the standing offer or walk away")
        th.update(round=th["round"] + 1, timeouts=0, last_at=self.clock())
        th["messages"].append({**msg, "from": "buyer"})
        reply = self._answer(s, th, msg, sheets)
        self._settle(s, "no_deal")
        return {**reply, "result": _public(s["result"])} if s["result"] else reply

    def attachment(self, team, sid, att):
        s = self.session(team, sid)
        if att not in s["files"]:
            raise Fail(404, "no such attachment in this session")
        kind, stated, standard = s["files"][att]
        if kind.endswith(".xlsx"):
            return xlsx(stated["unit_price"]), "application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet"
        fixed = s["case"].get("fixed_terms", {})
        if kind.startswith("order"):
            return pdf("Order confirmation", [("Agreed terms", {**fixed, **standard, **stated})]), "application/pdf"
        rest = {k: v for k, v in standard.items() if k not in stated}
        sections = [
            ("Offered terms", stated),
            ("Our standard terms (apply to everything not stated above)", rest),
            ("Terms fixed by your enquiry", fixed),
        ]
        return pdf("Quote - simulated supplier", sections), "application/pdf"

    def state(self, team, sid):
        s, now = self.session(team, sid), self.clock()
        threads = {
            k: {
                "offer_id": t["offer_id"],
                "status": t["status"],
                "closed": t["closed"],
                "offers": t["round"] - t["timeouts"],
                "seconds_left": None
                if t["closed"] or self.no_clock
                else max(0.0, round(t["last_at"] + MOVE_S - now, 1)),
            }
            for k, t in s["threads"].items()
        }
        out = {
            "session_id": sid,
            "case_id": s["case"]["case_id"],
            "set": "practice",
            "status": s["status"],
            "end_reason": s["end_reason"],
            "threads": threads,
            "rounds": sum(t["round"] for t in s["threads"].values()),
            "opening": {k: structured(t["messages"][0], 0) for k, t in s["threads"].items()},
            "moves": s["moves"],
        }
        if s["result"]:
            out.update(result={**s["result"], "trace": s["trace"]}, replay_url=f"/replay/{sid}")
        return out

    def thread(self, team, sid, sup):
        th = self.session(team, sid)["threads"].get(sup)
        if th is None:
            raise Fail(404, f"{sup} is not a supplier in this case")
        return {
            "supplier_id": sup,
            "offer_id": th["offer_id"],
            "status": th["status"],
            "closed": th["closed"],
            "messages": th["messages"],
            "timeouts": th["late"],
        }

    def board(self):
        rows = []
        for team, name in self.teams.items():
            best, ended = {}, [s for s in self._mine(team) if s["result"]]
            for s in ended:
                best[s["case"]["case_id"]] = max(best.get(s["case"]["case_id"], 0), s["result"]["score"])
            total = round(100 * sum(best.values()) / len(self.cases), 1)
            deals, rounds = (
                sum(s["result"]["deal"] for s in ended),
                sum(self.state(team, s["id"])["rounds"] for s in ended),
            )
            rows.append({"team_name": name, "played": len(best), "total": total, "deals": deals, "rounds": rounds})
        rows.sort(key=lambda r: -r["total"])
        teams = [{**r, "rank": i} for i, r in enumerate(rows, 1)]
        return {"set": "practice", "cases": len(self.cases), "window": None, "teams": teams}


def _public(result):
    return {k: v for k, v in result.items() if k != "trace"}
