play <case> [--agent naive|llm] [--seed N] [-v]   one negotiation against a twin, printed
"""

import argparse
import json
import logging
import os

from arena_kit.cli import load_env
from arena_kit.data import DataPackage
from arena_kit.play import play

from . import twins
from .table import LocalTable


def package():
    return DataPackage(os.environ.get("ARENA_DATA", "data/package"))


def agent_for(name, pkg):
    from .strategies import registry

    return registry(pkg)[name]()


def tournament(a):
    import gzip
    import time
    from pathlib import Path

    from . import tournament as t

    stamp = time.strftime("%Y%m%d-%H%M")
    out = Path("runs/lab") / f"{stamp}-{a.cmd}{'-' + a.label if a.label else ''}"
    t0 = time.time()
    if a.cmd == "compare":
        rows = t.compare(a.strategies, a.invented, a.seeds, a.workers, a.invent_seed)
        title = f"Lab compare {stamp}: {' vs '.join(a.strategies)}"
        min_scen = 0
    else:
        rows = t.search(a.minutes, a.invented, a.start, a.seeds, a.workers, a.invent_seed, a.seed)
        title = f"Lab search {stamp}: {a.minutes:g} min, {a.start} random variants to start"
        min_scen = len({r["scenario"] for r in rows})
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    text = t.report(rows, title, min_scenarios=min_scen)
    text += f"\nRun: `uv run python -m sellm.lab {' '.join(__import__('sys').argv[1:])}`, {time.time() - t0:.0f} s.\n"
    (out / "report.md").write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
    with gzip.open(out / "rows.jsonl.gz", "wt", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        for r in rows:
            f.write(json.dumps({k: v for k, v in r.items() if k != "trace"}, default=str) + "\n")
    best = sorted(t.summarise(rows, min_scen).values(), key=lambda x: -x["mean"])[:10]
    (out / "best.json").write_text(json.dumps(best, indent=1, default=str) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    print(text)
    print(f"wrote {out}/")


def show(result, table):
    for sid, t in table.threads.items():
        print(f"--- {sid}")
        for m in t.messages:
            sheets = [s["terms"].get("unit_price") for s in m.get("term_sheets") or []]
            print(f"  supplier {m['status']:<12} {sheets}  {m['body'][:160]!r}")
    keep = ("end_reason", "deal", "supplier_id", "terms", "c_open", "c_deal", "c_best", "score")
    print(json.dumps({k: result.get(k) for k in keep}, indent=1, default=str))


def main(argv=None):
    load_env()
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="python -m sellm.lab")
    ap.add_argument("-v", "--verbose", action="store_true")
    sub = ap.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)
    sub.add_parser("calibrate")
    sub.add_parser("twins")
    b = sub.add_parser("backtest")
    b.add_argument("--fit", action="store_true")
    b.add_argument("--write", action="store_true", help="write runs/lab/BACKTEST.md")
    p = sub.add_parser("play")
    p.add_argument("case")
    p.add_argument("--agent", default="naive", choices=["naive", "llm", "calc"])
    p.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=0)
    for mode in ("compare", "search"):
        t = sub.add_parser(mode)
        if mode == "compare":
            t.add_argument("strategies", nargs="+")
        else:
            t.add_argument("--minutes", type=float, default=10)
            t.add_argument("--start", type=int, default=64, help="random variants in the first round")
            t.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=0)
        t.add_argument("--invented", type=int, default=150, help="invented scenarios next to the twins")
        t.add_argument("--invent-seed", type=int, default=1)
        t.add_argument("--seeds", type=int, default=2, help="runs per strategy and scenario")
        t.add_argument("--workers", type=int, default=None)
        t.add_argument("--label", default="")
    a = ap.parse_args(argv)
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO if a.verbose else logging.WARNING, format="%(message)s")

    if a.cmd == "calibrate":
        scenarios = twins.build(package())
        twins.save(scenarios)
        for s in scenarios:
            print(s.name, s.notes, {k: round(p.full_cost, 2) for k, p in s.personas.items()})
        print(f"wrote {twins.CACHE}")
    elif a.cmd == "twins":
        for s in twins.load():
            floors = {k: round(p.full_cost, 2) for k, p in s.personas.items()}
            print(f"{s.name:5} {s.case['type']:15} {s.case['buyer']['category_goal']:14} floors {floors}  {s.notes}")
    elif a.cmd == "backtest":
        from . import backtest

        pkg, scenarios = package(), twins.load()
        if a.fit:
            _, per, ranges = backtest.fit(scenarios, pkg.facts)
            for s in scenarios:
                for p in s.personas.values():
                    for k, v in per[s.name].items():
                        setattr(p, k, v)
                    p.ranges = {**ranges[s.name], "noise": [0.05, 0.1, 0.2]}
            twins.save(scenarios)
            print(f"wrote {twins.CACHE}")
        rows = backtest.evaluate(scenarios, pkg.facts)
        print(backtest.report(rows))
        if a.write:
            backtest.write_report(scenarios, rows, "runs/lab/BACKTEST.md")
            print("wrote runs/lab/BACKTEST.md")
    elif a.cmd in ("compare", "search"):
        tournament(a)
    elif a.cmd == "play":
        pkg = package()
        name = a.case.split(":")[-1]
        scenario = next(s for s in twins.load() if s.name == name)
        table = LocalTable(scenario, pkg.facts, seed=a.seed)
        result = play(table, scenario.case["case_id"], agent_for(a.agent, pkg))
        show(result, table)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# The lab from a shell, no Claude needed. Long runs go to the background and survive a closed terminal.
#   scripts/lab search 60              a 60-minute strategy search (any number of minutes)
#   scripts/lab compare naive calc     agents side by side (background)
#   scripts/lab stress calc            stress-test an agent: crashes, 422s, broken must-haves, ... (background)
#   scripts/lab status                 what is running, the newest progress lines, where the report is
#   scripts/lab stop                   stop a running lab run
#   scripts/lab play P01 [agent]       one negotiation, every e-mail printed (foreground)
#   scripts/lab <command> ...          anything else goes to 'python -m sellm.lab' (see --help)
# Extra options pass through, e.g. scripts/lab search 30 --mode sequential --label kitrunner
# Reports: runs/lab/<time>-<command>[-label]/report.md. Guide: sellm/lab/README.md.
set -uo pipefail

def _pkg():
    from arena_kit.data import DataPackage

    facts()  # skips without the data package
    return DataPackage(DATA.parent)


def test_scenarios_survive_a_round_trip(tmp_path):
    from sellm.lab import store

    path = tmp_path / "s.json.gz"
    store.save(SCENARIOS, path)
    back = store.load(path)
    assert [s.name for s in back] == [s.name for s in SCENARIOS]
    assert back[0].personas.keys() == SCENARIOS[0].personas.keys()


@pytest.mark.parametrize("mode", ["sequential", "parallel"])
def test_every_edge_case_is_playable_by_both_agents(mode):
    from sellm.lab.invent import EDGES, edge_suite
    from sellm.lab.strategies import Calculator
    from sellm.lab.table import play_lab

    pkg = _pkg()
    suite = edge_suite(pkg, per_edge=1, seed=300)
    assert {t for s in suite for t in s.tags} >= set(EDGES) - {"current_contract"}
    for s in suite:
        assert s.c_open > s.c_best
        for agent in (NaiveAgent(), Calculator(pkg)):
            table = LocalTable(s, pkg.facts, seed=1, clock=True, think_s=2.0, wave_cap_s=480)
            r = play_lab(table, agent, mode=mode)
            assert 0.0 <= r["score"] <= 1.0


def test_calculator_walks_away_when_the_alternative_is_best():
    from sellm.lab.invent import generate
    from sellm.lab.strategies import Calculator
    from sellm.lab.table import play_lab

    pkg = _pkg()
    for s in generate(3, pkg, seed=11, data_share=0.0, edges=["walk_away_best"]):
        r = play_lab(LocalTable(s, pkg.facts, seed=0), Calculator(pkg))
        assert r["score"] == pytest.approx(1.0) and not r["deal"]


def test_tournament_compare_runs_in_worker_processes(tmp_path):
    from sellm.lab import tournament

    _pkg()
    opts = {"clock": True, "mode": "parallel", "wave_cap_s": 480, "think_s": 2.0, "vary": True}
    run = tournament.Run(tmp_path / "run", opts, SCENARIOS[:4], SCENARIOS[4:6], workers=2, log=lambda _: None)
    try:
        rows = tournament.compare(run, ["naive", "calc"], seeds=1)
    finally:
        run.close()
    assert len(rows) == 2 * 6 and not [r for r in rows if "crash" in r]
    text = tournament.report(rows, "test")
    assert "| 1 | calc" in text or "| 1 | naive" in text


def test_stress_verdict_fails_on_a_broken_must_have():
    from sellm.lab import stress

    row = {"strategy": "x", "knobs": {}, "scenario": "S", "kind": "invented", "seed": 0, "type": "rfq",
           "goal": "routine", "tags": [], "archetypes": ["family"], "pool": "train", "score": 0.0,
           "deal": True, "broken": True, "worse": False, "wall_s": 0.1, "mode": "parallel"}  # fmt: skip
    _, verdict = stress.report([row], "x", {})
    assert verdict == "FAIL"
    _, verdict = stress.report([{**row, "broken": False}], "x", {})
    assert verdict == "PASS"
EOF

# The lab: test buyer strategies without spending practice quota

A local copy of the arena with simulated suppliers. Any agent with `decide(case, threads)` plays
against it exactly as against the arena (the kit's `RemoteTable` interface), for free, a few hundred
negotiations per second on a laptop. No arena calls, no LLM calls unless you choose the `llm` agent.

**What it is good for:** ranking strategy variants by their mean over many scenarios; finding the
mistakes that cost points in the final (crashes, refused moves, broken must-haves, deals worse than
the opening, timeouts in RFQs, running out of time). **What it is not:** a prediction of one case's
score. A lab winner is a hypothesis until the sandbox (`case:D01`, `case:D02`, free) or one practice
case confirms it.

## Quick start

```bash
scripts/lab play P01                  # one negotiation against the P01 twin, every e-mail printed
scripts/lab play X01-007 naive        # a generated scenario, the kit's naive agent
scripts/lab compare naive calc        # agents side by side (background, ~1 min)
scripts/lab search 60                 # a 60-minute search for the best Calculator knobs (background)
scripts/lab stress calc               # stress test: everything the final may bring (background)
scripts/lab status                    # what is running, newest progress, where the report is
scripts/lab stop                      # stop a run
```

Every run writes `runs/lab/<time>-<command>[-label]/`: `report.md` (read this), `best.json` (the ten
best variants with their knobs), `progress.log` (live). Raw rows and scenarios are git-ignored.
Commit `report.md` and `best.json` of runs that matter and log them as `[run]` (AGENTS.md).

Use a result: `--knobs runs/lab/<run>/best.json` (rank 1) or `...best.json#3` (rank 3), e.g.
`scripts/lab stress calc --knobs runs/lab/<run>/best.json`. Your own agent: `--agent module:Class`
(constructed with the data package if it takes one), e.g. `scripts/lab compare calc sellm.agent:SellmAgent`.

## Options (all commands that play)

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--mode parallel\|sequential` | parallel | one loop per thread (what our final runner must do) / the kit's `play()` (one thread at a time; RFQ threads time out) |
| `--no-clock` | off | no simulated time: no timeouts, no wave cap |
| `--wave-cap S` | 480 | seconds per case, as a Live Final wave; the runner closes 90 s before it with the kit's `closing_move` |
| `--think S` | 2.0 | our seconds per move; `-1` = the real time the agent took (use for LLM agents) |
| `--fixed-twins` | off | the fitted twins only; by default each run draws a member of each twin's family |
| `--invented N`, `--test N` | 160, 80 | generated scenarios for training and for the unseen test |
| `--seeds N` | 2 | runs per strategy and scenario |

## Reading a report

- Rank by **Test**: scenarios the search never tuned on (held-out twins P04, P10, P18 plus fresh
  generated ones). A big gap between Train and Test means the variant is fitted to the lab, not good.
- **Crash, 422, Broken, Worse** must be 0 for anything we run in the final. **Below alt**: ended
  under what walking away would have scored. **Wave cap**: ran out of time. **Timeouts**: threads
  left more than 60 s.
- The tables below the ranking break the winner down by case type, goal, supplier archetype and edge
  case: that is where to look for the next improvement.

## How the suppliers are modelled

`persona.py` (the economics), `bot.py` (the decisions and e-mails), `table.py` (the arena's rules and
the clock). In short:

- A supplier accepts a package when its cash value to the supplier (price, payment at its cost of
  money, freight, chargebacks at its real defect rate, plus lever premiums such as overtime for a
  short lead time) reaches its floor, its full cost. For the twins the floor is calibrated so that
  the cheapest acceptable package costs exactly the case's known `C_best`.
- First counter: a share of (opening - floor). Then it gives back a share of each of our steps, up
  to a per-round limit that shrinks; nothing without a move from us; verified data of the kinds that
  move it takes off a little more; `final_offer` when its patience is used up; pushing price after
  that may end the thread. Noise, an approval ladder (one round on hold), `no_bid`, walking after an
  ultimatum, withdrawing when left waiting at a final offer.
- Cited data is checked by the arena's published rules (`claims.py`): verified, irrelevant,
  contradicted, duplicate; a letter and a contract are one argument across the e-mail.
- Tone, threats, leaks and questions are read by keyword (`reader.py`); `llm_reader` can replace that
  with an LLM. The lab does not understand an argument: results that rest on wording prove nothing.

Scenario kinds: **twins** of the 15 suppliers we have played (12 cases, built from `runs/`),
**case files** we never played (P06, P09, P12-P17, P19 with their real suppliers from the data), and
**invented** ones (any type, goal, field, must-have, RFQ; suppliers drawn from the 46 in the data;
eight archetypes from the brief; edge cases such as an opening that breaks a must-have, walking away
as the best move, short round limits, a bidder that does not bid, case-only facts, prices per 100).

## How good it is, and keeping it good

- `runs/lab/BACKTEST.md`: our real sessions replayed into the twins (mean error per reply under 1 %
  of the opening value, status right in about 9 of 10; weak on P05 and P10).
- `runs/lab/VALIDATION.md`: the same agent in lab and arena (kit LLM agent: practice mean 59.8 in the
  lab vs 61.5 in the arena; naive P01 0.590 vs 0.583).

After new practice or sandbox sessions were pulled (`scripts/pull-runs`):

```bash
uv run python -m sellm.lab calibrate              # floors from the new sessions
uv run python -m sellm.lab backtest --fit --write # dynamics and families, runs/lab/BACKTEST.md
uv run python -m sellm.lab validate               # naive agent lab vs arena (free); --llm costs calls
uv run pytest tests/test_lab.py                   # the lab's own tests
```

Then commit `sellm/lab/twins.json` and the reports.

## Options (all commands that play)

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--mode parallel\|sequential` | parallel | one loop per thread (what our final runner must do) / the kit's `play()` (one thread at a time; RFQ threads time out) |
| `--no-clock` | off | no simulated time: no timeouts, no wave cap |
| `--wave-cap S` | 480 | seconds per case, as a Live Final wave; the runner closes 90 s before it with the kit's `closing_move` |
| `--think S` | 2.0 | our seconds per move; `-1` = the real time the agent took (use for LLM agents) |
| `--fixed-twins` | off | the fitted twins only; by default each run draws a member of each twin's family |
| `--invented N`, `--test N` | 160, 80 | generated scenarios for training and for the unseen test |
| `--seeds N` | 2 | runs per strategy and scenario |

## Reading a report

- Rank by **Test**: scenarios the search never tuned on (held-out twins P04, P10, P18 plus fresh
  generated ones). A big gap between Train and Test means the variant is fitted to the lab, not good.
- **Crash, 422, Broken, Worse** must be 0 for anything we run in the final. **Below alt**: ended
  under what walking away would have scored. **Wave cap**: ran out of time. **Timeouts**: threads
  left more than 60 s.
- The tables below the ranking break the winner down by case type, goal, supplier archetype and edge
  case: that is where to look for the next improvement.

## How the suppliers are modelled

`persona.py` (the economics), `bot.py` (the decisions and e-mails), `table.py` (the arena's rules and
the clock). In short:

- A supplier accepts a package when its cash value to the supplier (price, payment at its cost of
  money, freight, chargebacks at its real defect rate, plus lever premiums such as overtime for a
  short lead time) reaches its floor, its full cost. For the twins the floor is calibrated so that
  the cheapest acceptable package costs exactly the case's known `C_best`.
- First counter: a share of (opening - floor). Then it gives back a share of each of our steps, up
  to a per-round limit that shrinks; nothing without a move from us; verified data of the kinds that
  move it takes off a little more; `final_offer` when its patience is used up; pushing price after
  that may end the thread. Noise, an approval ladder (one round on hold), `no_bid`, walking after an
  ultimatum, withdrawing when left waiting at a final offer.
- Cited data is checked by the arena's published rules (`claims.py`): verified, irrelevant,
  contradicted, duplicate; a letter and a contract are one argument across the e-mail.
- Tone, threats, leaks and questions are read by keyword (`reader.py`); `llm_reader` can replace that
  with an LLM. The lab does not understand an argument: results that rest on wording prove nothing.

**case files** we never played (P06, P09, P12-P17, P19 with their real suppliers from the data), and
**invented** ones (any type, goal, field, must-have, RFQ; suppliers drawn from the 46 in the data;
eight archetypes from the brief; edge cases such as an opening that breaks a must-have, walking away
as the best move, short round limits, a bidder that does not bid, case-only facts, prices per 100).

- `runs/lab/BACKTEST.md`: our real sessions replayed into the twins (mean error per reply under 1 %
  of the opening value, status right in about 9 of 10; weak on P05 and P10).
- `runs/lab/VALIDATION.md`: the same agent in lab and arena (kit LLM agent: practice mean 59.8 in the
  lab vs 61.5 in the arena; naive P01 0.590 vs 0.583).

```bash

uv run python -m sellm.lab backtest --fit --write # dynamics and families, runs/lab/BACKTEST.md
uv run python -m sellm.lab validate               # naive agent lab vs arena (free); --llm costs calls
uv run pytest tests/test_lab.py                   # the lab's own tests
```

Then commit `sellm/lab/twins.json` and the reports.

class Stepper:
    """Jonathan's sandbox probe h2/h8/h10 (experiments/sandbox_probes.py) as an agent: fixed terms,
    open at `start`, raise by `step` per e-mail while staying 0.30 below the supplier, accept as soon
    as it stops saying `open` (at most 8 e-mails)."""

    def __init__(self, start, step, fixed, margin=0.3, max_messages=8):
        self.ask, self.step, self.fixed, self.margin, self.max = start, step, fixed, margin, max_messages
        self.sent = 0

    def decide(self, case, threads):
        from arena_kit.play import latest, standing

        sid = case["suppliers"][0]
        events = threads[sid]
        status = latest(events).get("status")
        sheet_id, terms = standing(events)
        if self.sent and (status != "open" or self.sent >= self.max):
            return {"supplier_id": sid, "message": {"action": {"type": "accept", "term_sheet_id": sheet_id}}}
        if self.sent:
            self.ask = round(max(self.ask, min(self.ask + self.step, terms["unit_price"] - self.margin)), 2)
        self.sent += 1
        sheet = {**self.fixed, "unit_price": self.ask}
        return {"supplier_id": sid, "message": {"body": "We can improve our proposal.", "term_sheets": [{"terms": sheet}]}}


# experiments/RESULTS.md section 3: D01, 30 days, 24 months, start February

    ("open 48.00, steps 0.40", 48.0, 0.40, [0.88, 0.90]),
]

    arena did? Returns rows (label, arena range, lab mean, lab spread)."""

    return rows

content.text:
Fertig. Die Testumgebung ist ausgebaut, verbraucht keinen der 189 Versuche und ist komplett gepusht (`aa098d5`). Einen großen Such- oder Stresslauf habe ich wie gewünscht noch nicht gestartet, nur kurze Funktionsproben.

## Was neu ist

1. **Realistischere Supplier:**
   - 8 Typen aus dem Brief: Familienbetrieb, Konzern mit Chef-Freigabe, Lohnfertiger mit Geldknappheit, Beinahe-Monopolist, Händler, Qualitätsproblem, Kapazitätsengpass, großzügig.
   - Zufallsstreuung, `no_bid`, Abbruch bei Drohungen, Rückfragen nach Daten.
   - Lieferplan und 8D-Bericht als Anhänge.
   - Optional ein LLM, das unsere Mails liest (`--reader llm`, kostet Aufrufe).
2. **Uhr wie im Finale:** Antworten nach 20–60 s, 60-Sekunden-Timeouts mit neuer Angebots-ID, 8 Minuten pro Welle. Zwei Spielweisen: ein Thread nach dem anderen (`play()` im Kit) oder eine Schleife pro Thread.
3. **Szenarien für alles, was kommen kann:**
   - Twins unserer 15 Supplier, jeweils als Familie plausibler Varianten.
   - Die 9 nie gespielten Practice-Fälle mit ihren echten Suppliern.
   - Erfundene Fälle aller 7 Typen mit jedem verhandelbaren Feld und 12 Grenzfällen.
4. **Turnier mit Kontrollgruppe:** Die Suche stimmt auf einem Pool ab, gewertet wird auf ungesehenen Szenarien. Dazu Fehlerbalken, ein paarweiser Test ("klar besser" oder "nicht unterscheidbar") und eine Aufschlüsselung, wo die Strategie schwach ist.
5. **Stresstest:** Er schlägt Alarm bei Absturz, abgelehntem Zug oder verletzter Pflichtbedingung.

## Wie gut das Lab vorhersagt

- **Strategie-Rangfolge:** Jonathans 5 Sandbox-Strategien landen im Lab in derselben Reihenfolge, und jedes Ergebnis liegt im echten Bereich (zum Beispiel 0,881 gegen 0,88–0,90).
- **Einzelne Antworten:** Im Schnitt 0,77 % daneben, der Status stimmt in 217 von 237 Fällen.
- **LLM-Agent des Kits:** 59,8 im Lab gegen 61,5 in der Arena.

Perfekt vorhersagen kann es nicht. Bei P05 und P10 ist es schwach, und Argumente versteht es ohne `--reader llm` nicht. Ein Sieger im Lab muss deshalb immer noch in der kostenlosen Sandbox bestätigt werden.

## Was das Lab schon gefunden hat

- **RFQ mit dem Runner aus dem Kit:** Die Threads laufen in Timeouts, und ein veraltetes Angebot führt zu einem 422-Absturz. Der Runner fürs Finale braucht deshalb eine Schleife pro Thread. Das steht für das Team in `STATUS.md`.
- **Unsere Strategie hat Deals über dem Startangebot angenommen** (0 Punkte), weil sie den Beziehungsabschlag nicht kannte. Behoben, jetzt sind es 0 von 324.
- **Meine eigene "Verbesserung" bei kurzen Rundenlimits kostete 4,9 Punkte.** Das Lab hat sie widerlegt, ich habe sie zurückgenommen.

## Was die anderen gemacht haben

Omar hat unseren Agenten als `--agent sellm` eingebunden. Er nutzt die beste Lab-Strategie, alle Tests laufen damit zusammen (74 grün). Jonathans Sandbox-Ergebnisse sind in das Modell eingeflossen.

## Selbst starten, ohne mich

```bash
scripts/lab stress sellm.agent:make_agent   # zuerst: muss PASS ergeben
scripts/lab search 60                       # 1 h Suche im Hintergrund
scripts/lab status                          # Fortschritt ansehen
scripts/lab play P01                        # eine Verhandlung lesen
```

Berichte landen unter `runs/lab/<zeit>-…/report.md`, die Anleitung steht in `sellm/lab/README.md`.

Mein Vorschlag als Nächstes: den Stresstest für den sellm-Agenten laufen lassen, dann 1 h suchen, dann den Sieger kostenlos in der Sandbox auf D01 und D02 prüfen. Soll ich damit loslegen?

  - **Export:** `report.md`, `best.json`, `rows.csv` (eine Zeile pro Verhandlung, für Excel) oder der ganze Lauf als ZIP.
- **Play one:** Eine einzelne Verhandlung mit beliebigem Agenten und Szenario. Du siehst jede Mail beider Seiten.

## Was ich insgesamt gebaut habe

1. **Ein lokales Lab statt der echten Arena:** Supplier-Bots, die sich fast wie die echten verhalten. Dahinter stehen ihre Untergrenze aus `C_best`, die Art, wie sie unsere Schritte spiegeln, `final_offer`, Abbruch, Chef-Freigabe, Timeouts und die 8-Minuten-Grenze.

3. **Werkzeuge:** Suche nach der besten Strategie, Vergleich mit statistischem Test, Stresstest und Backtest gegen die Realität. Alles startbar über die Oberfläche oder `scripts/lab`.

## Wie uns das nützt

- **Strategien testen kostet keine Quota mehr.** Eine Stunde Suche ersetzt tausende Practice-Versuche. Die 189 Versuche bleiben komplett für die Bestätigung und den Sonntag.

Kurz gesagt: Das Lab bringt uns im Finale noch keinen nachgewiesenen Punkt. Es hat aber Fehler gefunden, die uns Punkte gekostet hätten, und es lässt uns mit der Quota gezielt statt blind testen.

## Was es schon gebracht hat

1. **Ein Fehler in unserem Final-Agenten, der Fälle auf 0 gesetzt hätte, ist behoben.** Er hat in 2–4 von 324 Verhandlungen Deals angenommen, die teurer als das Startangebot waren, weil er den Beziehungsabschlag nicht kannte. Jetzt sind es 0.
2. **Ein Risiko für eine ganze Welle ist aufgedeckt.** Der Runner des Kits spielt RFQ-Threads nacheinander. Dabei laufen andere Threads in Timeouts, und bei einem veralteten Angebot stürzt der Fall ab. Kommt im Finale eine RFQ-Welle und wir nutzen diesen Runner, verlieren wir dort Punkte. Behoben ist das noch nicht: Wir brauchen einen Runner mit einer Schleife pro Thread.
3. **Unser Agent `--agent sellm` hat seine Einstellungen aus dem Lab.** Dort ist er +8,8 Punkte besser als die Standardeinstellung und +25 besser als der naive Agent, ungefähr auf dem Niveau des LLM-Agenten des Kits, aber ohne LLM-Kosten und ohne LLM-Ausfälle.
4. **Eine schlechte Idee ist früh gestoppt.** Eine plausible Änderung hätte 4,9 Punkte gekostet; das Lab hat das in einer Minute gezeigt.
5. **Alle 189 Versuche sind noch da.**

## Was es uns ab jetzt bringt

- **Jeder Practice-Versuch bestätigt eine Hypothese, statt zu raten.** Wir testen 1.000 Varianten lokal und spielen nur die beste in der Arena.
- **Vorbereitung auf unbekannte Fälle:** Der Stresstest prüft unseren Agenten auf alle Falltypen und Grenzfälle, bevor das Finale sie bringt.
- **Sonntag 08:00:** Nach dem Daten-Update können wir in Minuten neu prüfen, ob noch alles läuft.
- **Für die Jury:** Ein validiertes Lab, das echte Ergebnisse nachweislich vorhersagt, ist eine starke Geschichte für die Bewertung von Vorgehen und Nachvollziehbarkeit.

## Was es nicht kann

Es verhandelt nicht für uns und garantiert keine Punktzahl. Ob `sellm` in der echten Arena wirklich mit dem LLM-Agenten mithält, wissen wir erst nach dem Test in der Sandbox.

## Damit es sich in Punkte übersetzt

1. **Stresstest für den Final-Agenten** (`scripts/lab stress sellm.agent:make_agent`, etwa 2 Minuten): Er muss PASS ergeben.
2. **Kostenloser Gegencheck in der Sandbox:** `sellm` gegen den LLM-Agenten des Kits auf D01 und D02. Erst damit wissen wir, ob die Lab-Vorteile echt sind.
3. **Einen Runner mit einer Schleife pro Thread für RFQs** bauen, das betrifft das ganze Team.
4. **Danach 1 h Suche** und die Gewinner auf 2–3 Practice-Fällen bestätigen.

Soll ich mit 1 und 2 anfangen? Die Sandbox kostet keine Quota.

content.text:
Lokal findest du schnell und gratis heraus, *was* sich zu testen lohnt. Die Arena brauchst du dann nur noch, um die 2–3 besten Kandidaten zu bestätigen. Ohne das Lab müsstest du in der Arena suchen, und das geht praktisch nicht:

| | Arena (Practice, Sandbox) | Lokal (Lab) |
|---|---|---|
| Dauer pro Verhandlung | 3–5 Minuten (der Supplier antwortet nach 20–60 s) | Millisekunden |
| Menge | Practice: noch 189 Versuche für alles bis zum Finale. Sandbox: kostenlos, aber nur 2 Fälle | Im 10-Minuten-Lauf heute 27.800 Verhandlungen, also rund 150.000 pro Stunde |
| Fälle | 10 Practice-Fälle, 2 Sandbox-Fälle | Alle 7 Falltypen, 46 Supplier, Grenzfälle, auch solche, die das Finale bringen kann |
| Aussagekraft | Ein Lauf ist Zufall, weil Supplier nicht immer gleich antworten | Hunderte Szenarien mit Fehlerbalken: ob A wirklich besser als B ist |
| Einblick | Nur Ergebnis und Begründungen | Alles sichtbar: die versteckte Untergrenze, warum ein Deal schlecht war, wo genau es hakt |
| Fehler | Kosten einen echten Versuch oder einen Fall im Finale | Kosten nichts |

**Ein Beispiel von heute:** Jonathan hat 15 Minuten und 20 Sandbox-Sessions gebraucht, um eine einzige Frage zu klären, nämlich die Schrittgröße. Das Lab hat sein Ergebnis in Sekunden nachgestellt und danach in 10 Minuten 64 Strategie-Varianten auf 162 Szenarien verglichen. In der Arena wären das tausende Versuche gewesen; wir haben 189.

**So greifen beide ineinander:**
1. **Lokal:** 1.000 Ideen rein, die 3 besten raus. Schlechte Ideen und Fehler fliegen gratis raus.
2. **Sandbox (gratis) und Practice (Quota):** Prüfen, ob die 3 auch in echt gut sind.
3. **Ergebnis zurück ins Lab:** Jede echte Session macht die Twins genauer, und die nächste lokale Suche wird treffsicherer.

content.text:
**Teilweise ja.** Kurze Runden mit Hypothese, Lab-Test und dann übernehmen oder verwerfen sind richtig für die *Entscheidungslogik*: welche Bedingungen wir fordern, wie groß die Schritte sind, wann wir annehmen, wie wir RFQs führen. Genau so habe ich heute die schlechte Idee mit den Rundenlimits in einer Minute verworfen. Als *Hauptstrategie* wäre "viele Runden, viel anpassen" aber nicht das Beste. Dafür gibt es drei Gründe.

## Warum nicht nur das

1. **Wir würden den Simulator optimieren, nicht die Arena.** Das Lab beruht auf 15 Suppliern und gut 40 echten Sessions. Wer endlos daran feilt, gewinnt Lab-Punkte, die in der Arena nicht existieren. Deshalb gilt: Jede Änderung muss auf den ungesehenen Testszenarien klar besser sein (mehr als zwei Standardfehler), und Gewinner werden gebündelt in der Sandbox bestätigt.
2. **Das Lab versteht keine Argumente.** Laut Brief versteht der Supplier, was wir schreiben, und es hat Folgen. Den größten Spielraum haben P08, P18 und P10, 10–31 % über der Untergrenze. Der liegt wahrscheinlich in den Daten und Argumenten, also Notizen, Briefen und News der Supplier, und genau das kann das Lab nicht bewerten.
3. **Feintuning der Knobs bringt nur noch wenige Punkte.** Woanders liegt mehr:
   - Der RFQ-Runner kann eine ganze Welle kosten.
   - Die 8-Minuten-Grenze muss passen.
   - Unbekannte Falltypen müssen robust laufen.

## Passt das zu dem, was wir bauen sollen?

Die Aufgabe ist ein KI-Einkaufsagent, der per E-Mail verhandelt, die Daten liest, Angebote berechnet und im Finale ohne Menschen auf unbekannten Fällen spielt. Tacto rät: *"Numbers come from code, the model writes."* Unser `sellm` erfüllt im Moment nur die erste Hälfte:

| Teil | Stand |
|---|---|
| Zahlen und Entscheidungen im Code (Calculator) | ✅ vorhanden, im Lab validiert |
| Robustheit (Pflichtbedingungen, kein Absturz, kein Deal schlechter als das Startangebot) | ✅ im Lab geprüft |
| **Schreiben mit LLM** (Ton, Argumente, Antworten auf Rückfragen) | ❌ fehlt, die Mails sind Vorlagen |
| **Supplier lesen** (Steckbrief je Supplier aus Notizen, Briefen, News) | ❌ fehlt (Arbeitspaket B) |
| **Runner mit Schleife pro Thread** und Zeitbudget fürs Finale | ❌ fehlt (Arbeitspaket C) |

Das Lab ist also der **Prüfstand**, nicht das Produkt. Es passt zum Ziel, wenn es dafür dient, den Rechenteil und die Robustheit abzusichern, während das Team den LLM-Teil und den Runner baut. Für die Jury ist das eine gute Geschichte: Entscheidungen im Code, die gegen echte Ergebnisse validiert sind, und ein LLM, das sie formuliert.

## Was ich empfehle

- **Lab-Schleifen ja, aber begrenzt.** Jede Runde testet eine aufgeschriebene Hypothese und wird übernommen, wenn sie auf den Testszenarien klar besser ist. Gewinner gehen alle paar Stunden in die Sandbox. Nach jeder echten Session werden die Twins neu kalibriert.
- **Mehr Zeit geht in die drei Lücken oben.** Sie bringen vermutlich mehr Punkte als weiteres Feintuning. Es sind noch ungefähr 18 Stunden bis zum Freeze.
- **Das Lab prüft jeden neuen Baustein**, zum Beispiel den LLM-Schreiber oder den neuen Runner, mit dem Stresstest, bevor er in die Arena geht.

Welche der Lücken du oder ich übernehmen, solltet ihr im Team kurz absprechen. Omar arbeitet bereits am Agenten-Einstieg, und Jonathan hatte die Arbeitspakete in `PLAN.md` vorgeschlagen.

Three groups, one person each, each with its own agent sessions. Claim one in `docs/STATUS.md`.
Each group owns its files; the groups meet only at four interfaces: `make_agent` with its
`fallback` (`sellm/agent.py`), `dossier()`, `citable_for()` and `arguments()` (section 10).

Du hast recht. Ich habe die Supplier als Regel-Engine mit Textvorlagen gebaut, das LLM war nur ein Zusatz zum Lesen der Mails. Das entspricht nicht der echten Arena, und du hattest ausdrücklich gesagt, dass wir LLM-Tokens dafür einsetzen dürfen. Das baue ich jetzt richtig.

**Wie die echte Arena laut Brief arbeitet:** Harte Grenzen kommen aus den Zahlen des Suppliers (Untergrenze, Freigabe durch den Chef, nichts ohne Gegenzug). Innerhalb dieser Grenzen entscheidet er "wie die Person, die er ist" und liest dafür die ganze Mail. Die Dokumente werden aus seinem Zustand erzeugt.

**Genau so baue ich den neuen LLM-Supplier:**
1. **Die kalibrierte Engine** liefert die harten Grenzen und den Spielraum für diese Runde: Untergrenze, maximales Zugeständnis, Chef-Freigabe, Geduld.
2. **Das LLM (dein OpenAI-Key)** spielt die Person:
   - Es liest unsere komplette Mail mit Konditionsblättern und Prüfergebnissen der zitierten Daten.
   - Es kennt die echte Vorgeschichte des Suppliers aus dem Datenpaket: Briefe, Gesprächsnotizen, News und frühere Verhandlungen.
   - Es entscheidet, wie weit es nachgibt, ob es kontert, zustimmt, ein letztes Angebot macht oder abbricht, und welche Struktur es anbietet.
   - Es schreibt die Antwort in seinem eigenen Ton.
3. **Der Code** rechnet die Preise und erzeugt die Konditionsblätter und Dokumente. Er erzwingt die Grenzen, sodass das LLM nie unter die Untergrenze gehen kann, wie in der echten Arena.
4. **Messung statt Behauptung:** Der LLM-Supplier durchläuft denselben Backtest gegen die 237 echten Antworten und Jonathans Sandbox-Proben, und wir sehen, ob er besser trifft als die Engine.

Ehrlicherweise: "Perfekt" im Sinne von identisch mit Tactos geheimem Bot geht nicht, weil wir dessen Prompts nicht kennen. Aber so nah wie möglich und messbar, das geht. Ich lege los und schaue mir zuerst an, was das Datenpaket pro Supplier an Texten hat:

"""LLM suppliers: the calibrated engine sets the hard limits, an LLM plays the person inside them.

That is how the brief describes the arena's suppliers: "Its hard limits come from its own situation:
it never sells below its cost floor, bigger moves need the boss's approval, data you cite is checked
by ID, and it gives nothing without a move from you. Inside those limits it decides as that person
would - reading your whole e-mail."

Per reply:
1. The engine (`bot.SupplierThread`, calibrated on our real sessions) works out its own move on a
   shadow copy: claim results, tone, the step we made, its concession, approval, patience.
2. Code turns that into bounds for this round: the lowest price the person may go to (never below
   the floor; at most a bit beyond the engine's move, more when we brought verified data), whether
   it must stay at a final offer, whether walking away is plausible.
3. The LLM, given the company (register facts, archetype, cost of money, capacity, quality), its
   history with Hollerau (letters, call and meeting notes, news, past renewals), this case and the
   thread so far, reads our e-mail and decides: counter, agree, final offer, hold or walk away, the
   price, a variant it prefers, which documents to attach, and writes the e-mail.
4. Code enforces the bounds, computes every number, renders the term sheets and documents (as the
   arena does: "never written by a language model"). If the LLM fails the engine's reply is used and
   counted (`llm_fail` in the result) - never silently.
"""

import copy
import hashlib
import json
import logging
import os
import re
import time
from pathlib import Path

from .bot import NAMES, SupplierThread, fmt
from .reader import read

log = logging.getLogger("arena")
CACHE = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "runs" / "lab" / "llm-cache"
ARCHETYPE_TEXT = {
    "family": "a family-owned company; the owner or a long-serving sales person writes. You remember how the "
    "buyer treated you, value loyalty and respect, dislike pressure, and are proud of your craft.",
    "group": "part of a larger group with an approval ladder; you are a sales manager who needs your managing "
    "director's sign-off for bigger moves. Formal, process-driven, careful with precedents.",
    "job_shop": "a small owner-run job shop that needs cash and work; informal, quick, flexible on terms, "
    "very interested in fast payment and steady orders.",
    "monopolist": "one of very few qualified sources; you barely move on price, say so politely, and do not "
    "fear losing the business.",
    "trader": "a stockist or trader whose margin depends on material prices; you insist on index clauses for "
    "longer terms and talk about material costs.",
    "quality": "a supplier with a quality problem the buyer knows about; you are defensive about defects but "
    "want to keep the business, and quality commitments cost you real money.",
    "capacity": "a supplier whose capacity is tight; short lead times and extra volume cost you overtime, and "
    "you prioritise customers who commit.",
    "generous": "a supplier hungry for this business; you move readily when the buyer moves.",
    "twin": "",
}
SYSTEM = """You play the person at a supplier who answers a buyer's e-mails in a B2B negotiation. The buyer is
Hollerau Pumpenwerke GmbH, a German pump maker. Stay in character: your company, your situation, your
history with Hollerau, as given below. Decide as that person would, reading the buyer's whole e-mail:
its term sheets, its arguments and data, its questions, its tone.

Hard limits you never break (they come from your company's economics and authority):
- Never quote a price below LOWEST_ALLOWED for this round (your floor or your boss's limit for one step).
- Give nothing without a move from the buyer, a convincing argument, or verified data.
- A final offer is final: once you said it, you do not go lower; you accept if the buyer meets it.
- Never reveal your costs, floor or margin unless your company is open about costs (see below).

Reply with ONE JSON object, nothing else:
{"decision": "counter" | "agree" | "final_offer" | "hold" | "walk_away",
 "price": <unit price in EUR on the buyer's best sheet's terms, or on "terms" if you change them>,
 "terms": {<optional: terms of the buyer's best sheet you will not accept, with the value you offer instead>},
 "alternative": {<optional: ONE term changed your way for a second package at the same value to you>},
 "attach": [<optional: "cost_breakdown" | "delivery_schedule" | "8d_report">],
 "email": "<your reply, 50-150 words, in your voice; write {PRICE} where your price goes and {ALT_PRICE}
          for the alternative's price; no other prices or percentages than those given to you>",
 "reasons": ["<2-4 short internal reasons for your decision>"]}

decision: counter = a new offer (price at or above LOWEST_ALLOWED); agree = you accept the buyer's best sheet
as it stands (only if it is at or above LOWEST_ALLOWED); final_offer = a counter you mark as your last word;
hold = you keep your current offer; walk_away = you end the talks (only when the buyer has been hostile,
threatened you, or pushes after your final offer)."""


def _complete_json():
    """An LLM call returning parsed JSON: OpenAI-compatible endpoints with JSON mode, else the kit's."""
    import httpx

    provider = os.environ.get("LLM_PROVIDER", "openai")
    model = os.environ.get("LAB_SUPPLIER_MODEL") or os.environ.get("LLM_MODEL")
    if provider != "openai":
        from arena_kit.agents.llm import llm_from_env, parse

        complete = llm_from_env()
        return lambda system, user: parse(complete(system, user))
    base = os.environ.get("LLM_BASE_URL", "https://api.openai.com/v1").rstrip("/")
    headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ.get('LLM_API_KEY', '')}"}
    client = httpx.Client(timeout=90.0)

    def call(system, user):
        body = {
            "model": model,
            "messages": [{"role": "system", "content": system}, {"role": "user", "content": user}],
            "response_format": {"type": "json_object"},
        }
        for attempt in range(4):
            r = client.post(f"{base}/chat/completions", json=body, headers=headers)
            if r.status_code == 400 and "response_format" in r.text and "response_format" in body:
                body.pop("response_format")
                continue
            if r.status_code in (429, 500, 502, 503, 504) and attempt < 3:
                time.sleep(float(r.headers.get("retry-after", 2 ** attempt)))
                continue
            r.raise_for_status()
            text = r.json()["choices"][0]["message"]["content"]
            return json.loads(re.search(r"\{.*\}", text, re.S).group(0))
        raise RuntimeError("LLM call failed after retries")

    return call


class Brain:
    """The LLM behind the suppliers of a process, with a disk cache (same prompt, same answer)."""

    def __init__(self, cache=True):
        self.call, self.cache = _complete_json(), cache
        self.calls = self.cached = self.failed = 0

    def ask(self, system, user):
        key = hashlib.sha256((system + "\n" + user).encode()).hexdigest()
        path = CACHE / f"{key}.json"
        if self.cache and path.exists():
            self.cached += 1
            return json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        self.calls += 1
        out = self.call(system, user)
        if self.cache:
            CACHE.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            path.write_text(json.dumps(out), encoding="utf-8")
        return out


def dossier(package, persona, case):
    """What the person knows about its own company and its history with Hollerau, from the data."""
    out, sid = [], persona.supplier_id
    if package is not None:
        intel = package.query("select * from supplier_intel where supplier_id = ?", (sid,))
        if intel:
            i = intel[0]
            out.append(
                f"Company: {persona.name}, {i.get('legal_form') or ''}, founded {i.get('founded')}, owner type "
                f"{i.get('owner_type')}{', group ' + i['group_parent'] if i.get('group_parent') else ''}, "
                f"{i.get('staff')} staff, turnover {i.get('turnover_band')}, equity ratio {i.get('equity_ratio_pct')} %, "
                f"credit index {i.get('credit_index')} (12 months ago {i.get('credit_index_12m_ago')}; higher is worse)."
            )
        hist = package.query(
            "select date, part_id, type, asked_pct, settled_pct, note from negotiation_history where supplier_id = ? "
            "order by date",
            (sid,),
        )
        if hist:
            out.append(
                "Past price rounds with Hollerau: "
                + "; ".join(
                    f"{h['date'][:7]} {h['type']}: asked {h['asked_pct']} %, settled {h['settled_pct']} %"
                    + (f" ({h['note']})" if h.get("note") else "")
                    for h in hist[-6:]
                    if h.get("asked_pct") is not None
                )
            )
        docs = package.query("select id, date, kind, subject from documents where supplier_id = ? order by date", (sid,))
        texts = []
        for d in docs[-8:]:
            try:
                body = package.document(d["id"])
            except (FileNotFoundError, ValueError):
                continue
            body = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", body.split("\n", 3)[-1])[:500]
            texts.append(f"[{d['date']} {d['kind']}: {d['subject']}] {body}")
        if texts:
            out.append("Letters, e-mails and notes about you (some written by the buyer's staff):\n" + "\n".join(texts))
        news = package.query("select date, headline, body from news where supplier_id = ? order by date", (sid,))
        if news:
            out.append("News about you: " + " | ".join(f"{n['date']} {n['headline']}" for n in news[-4:]))
    if persona.notes:
        out.append(f"What we know of your behaviour: {persona.notes}")
    return "\n".join(out)


def profile(persona, case, package):
    """The standing brief for the LLM: who it is and what its business needs."""
    b = case["buyer"]
    lines = [
        f"You are {persona.sender_name or 'the sales manager'} at {persona.name}.",
        ARCHETYPE_TEXT.get(persona.archetype, ""),
        f"Your style of writing: {persona.style} (family: warm, personal; corporate: formal; casual: short, direct).",
        f"The enquiry: {case['title']}. Parts: {', '.join(case['parts'])}. Need about {b['need_per_year']} pieces "
        f"a year. Negotiable: {', '.join(case['negotiable'])}. Fixed: {json.dumps(case.get('fixed_terms', {}))}.",
        f"Your own standard terms: {json.dumps({k: v for k, v in persona.standard.items() if k in NAMES})}.",
    ]
    rate = persona.rate
    if rate >= 0.15:
        lines.append(f"Cash is tight for you (your cost of money is about {rate:.0%} a year): faster payment is worth a lot to you.")
    elif rate <= 0.07:
        lines.append("Money is cheap for you: payment terms matter little to you, price matters.")
    if persona.premiums.get("lead_time_days"):
        lines.append("Your capacity is busy: a shorter lead time than your standard costs you overtime.")
    if persona.premiums.get("fixed_price"):
        lines.append("You carry material price risk: a fixed price without an index clause costs you a premium.")
    if persona.premiums.get("ppm_commitment"):
        lines.append(f"Your real defect rate is about {persona.ppm_real} ppm: a tighter quality commitment costs you money.")
    if persona.hard_limits:
        lines.append(f"Lines you do not cross: {json.dumps(persona.hard_limits)}.")
    lines.append("You are open about costs and may send a cost breakdown if asked." if persona.discloses else
                 "Your costs, margin and calculation stay internal; you do not send cost breakdowns.")  # fmt: skip
    if persona.claim_kinds:
        lines.append(f"Data that tends to convince you when verified: {', '.join(persona.claim_kinds)}.")
    history = dossier(package, persona, case)
    if history:
        lines.append(history)
    return "\n".join(x for x in lines if x)


def _sheet_text(terms):
    return ", ".join(f"{NAMES.get(k, k)} {fmt(k, v)}" for k, v in terms.items())


class LLMSupplierThread(SupplierThread):
    """A supplier thread whose replies an LLM writes and decides, inside the engine's bounds."""

    def __init__(self, persona, case, rng=None, session=None, brain=None, package=None):
        super().__init__(persona, case, rng, session)
        self.brain, self.package = brain, package
        self.brief = None
        self.llm_calls = self.llm_fail = 0

    def _brief(self):
        if self.brief is None:
            self.brief = profile(self.p, self.case, self.package)
        return self.brief

    def _shadow(self):
        """A copy that can run the engine without touching this thread or the session."""
        sh = copy.copy(self)
        sh.messages, sh.reasons, sh.history = list(self.messages), list(self.reasons), list(self.history)
        sh.rng = copy.deepcopy(self.rng)
        if self.session is not None:
            s = copy.copy(self.session)
            s.used, s.offers = set(self.session.used), dict(self.session.offers)
            sh.session = s
        return sh

    def respond(self, msg):
        if self.brain is None:
            return super().respond(msg)
        before = {k: getattr(self, k) for k in ("ask", "status", "round")}
        sh = self._shadow()
        engine = sh.respond(msg)  # the engine's own reply and the state after it
        try:
            out = self._decide(msg, engine, sh, before)
            self.llm_calls += 1
            return out
        except Exception as e:  # the engine's reply stands, and it is counted
            self.llm_fail += 1
            log.warning("LLM supplier failed (%s): the engine's reply is used", e)
            return self._adopt(sh, engine)

    def _adopt(self, sh, engine):
        """Take over the shadow's state and reply as this thread's own."""
        for k in ("ask", "status", "pressure", "mirror", "best_ours", "leaked", "warm", "counters", "timeouts",
                  "approved", "pending", "round", "closed", "standing"):  # fmt: skip
            setattr(self, k, getattr(sh, k))
        if self.session is not None:
            self.session.used |= sh.session.used
        self.history.append(engine)
        self.messages.append(engine)
        self.reasons.append(sh.reasons[-1])
        for ts in engine.get("term_sheets") or []:
            if self.session is not None:
                self.session.offers[ts["term_sheet_id"]] = (self.p.supplier_id, ts["terms"])
        return engine

    def _decide(self, msg, engine, sh, before):
        p, case = self.p, self.case
        sheets = [ts.get("terms", ts) for ts in msg.get("term_sheets") or []]
        best = max(sheets, key=lambda s: p.value(case, s)) if sheets else (self.standing or {}).get("terms")
        structure = {k: v for k, v in (best or {}).items() if k != "unit_price"}
        structure = p.nearest_allowed(case, structure)
        a, e, f = before["ask"], sh.ask, p.full_cost
        verified = [r for r in engine.get("claim_results") or [] if r["result"] == "verified"]
        feats = read(msg.get("body") or "")
        extra = 0.6 * max(0.0, a - e) + (0.1 * max(0.0, a - f) if verified else 0.0)
        if feats["appreciation"] and "family" in p.traits:
            extra += 0.03 * max(0.0, a - f)
        final_locked = before["status"] == "final_offer"
        lowest = a if final_locked else max(f, e - extra)

        def price_at(value, s=structure):
            return p.price_for(case, s, value)

        p_ask, p_engine, p_low = price_at(a), price_at(e), price_at(lowest)
        ours = {**structure, "unit_price": best["unit_price"]} if best and "unit_price" in best else None
        ours_value = p.value(case, best) if best else None
        thread = []
        for m in self.history[-8:]:
            who = "BUYER" if m.get("from") == "buyer" else f"YOU ({m.get('status')})"
            ts = "; ".join(_sheet_text(t.get("terms", t)) for t in m.get("term_sheets") or [])
            thread.append(f"{who}: {re.sub(chr(10) + '+', ' ', (m.get('body') or '')[:700])}" + (f"\n   sheets: {ts}" if ts else ""))
        claims = engine.get("claim_results") or []
        user = "\n".join([
            "THE NEGOTIATION SO FAR (oldest first):", *thread,
            "",
            f"THE BUYER'S NEW E-MAIL (their message {self.round} of {case.get('round_limit', 10)}):",
            msg.get("body") or "(no text)",
            "Their term sheets: " + (" | ".join(_sheet_text(s) for s in sheets) or "none (a question or a holding message)"),
            f"Data they cited, as checked against the records: {[c['result'] for c in claims] or 'none'}",
            "",
            "YOUR NUMBERS FOR THIS REPLY (on the terms of the buyer's best sheet: "
            f"{_sheet_text(structure) or 'its terms'}):",
            f"- your current offer is worth EUR {p_ask:.2f} on these terms",
            f"- LOWEST_ALLOWED this round: EUR {p_low:.2f}" + (" (you are at your final offer)" if final_locked else ""),
            f"- a typical move for you now would be EUR {p_engine:.2f}",
            f"- the buyer offers EUR {best['unit_price']:.2f}" if ours else "- the buyer sent no price",
            f"- your status so far: {before['status']}; your patience: {'running out' if sh.pressure >= p.patience - 1 else 'fine'}",
            "- a bigger move than usual needs your boss's approval" if p.approval_at and not self.approved else "",
            f"- the engine's own decision would be: {engine['status']}",
        ])  # fmt: skip
        d = self.brain.ask(SYSTEM + "\n\nWHO YOU ARE\n" + self._brief(), user)
        return self._apply(d, msg, engine, sh, before, structure, best, ours_value, lowest, final_locked)

    def _apply(self, d, msg, engine, sh, before, structure, best, ours_value, lowest, final_locked):
        p, case = self.p, self.case
        decision = str(d.get("decision", "counter")).lower()
        # the state the engine reached (pressure, mirror, claims used, ...), then our own move on it
        for k in ("pressure", "mirror", "best_ours", "leaked", "warm", "counters", "timeouts", "approved", "pending",
                  "round"):  # fmt: skip
            setattr(self, k, getattr(sh, k))
        if self.session is not None:
            self.session.used |= sh.session.used
        claims = engine.get("claim_results") or []
        attach = []
        for kind in d.get("attach") or []:
            if kind == "cost_breakdown" and p.discloses:
                from .bot import breakdown_text

                price = (self.standing or {}).get("terms", {}).get("unit_price") or p.opening["unit_price"]
                attach.append(("cost-breakdown", breakdown_text(p, price)))
            elif kind == "delivery_schedule":
                from .bot import schedule_text

                attach.append(("delivery-schedule", schedule_text(p, case, self.standing)))
            elif kind == "8d_report":
                from .bot import eight_d_text

                attach.append(("8d-report", eight_d_text(p, case)))
        feats = read(msg.get("body") or "")
        provoked = feats["ultimatum"] or feats["hostile"] or final_locked or self.round >= case.get("round_limit", 10) - 1
        if decision == "walk_away" and not provoked:
            decision = "final_offer" if self.round > 2 else "hold"
        if engine["status"] == "walked_away" and decision not in ("walk_away",):
            decision = "final_offer" if final_locked else decision  # the person may stay, as a final offer
        text = str(d.get("email") or "")
        reasons = [str(r) for r in d.get("reasons") or []][:4]
        if decision == "walk_away":
            self.closed, self.ask = "walked_away", before["ask"]
            return self._out("walked_away", [], text, reasons, claims, attach)
        if decision == "agree" and best and ours_value is not None and ours_value >= lowest - 1e-6 and p.allows(best):
            self.ask = min(before["ask"], max(lowest, ours_value))
            return self._out("agreed", [dict(best)], text, reasons, claims, attach, agreed=True)
        if decision == "hold" or (not msg.get("term_sheets") and decision != "final_offer"):
            self.ask = before["ask"]
            sheets = [self.standing["terms"]] if self.standing else []
            return self._out(before["status"], sheets, text, reasons, claims, attach)
        # counter or final offer: its price on its terms, kept inside the bounds
        terms = dict(structure)
        for k, v in (d.get("terms") or {}).items():
            options = case["term_options"].get(k) or []
            if k in terms and k != "unit_price" and (v in options or v == p.standard.get(k)):
                terms[k] = v
        terms = p.nearest_allowed(case, terms)
        try:
            price = float(d.get("price"))
        except (TypeError, ValueError):
            price = p.price_for(case, terms, sh.ask)
        value = p.value(case, {**terms, "unit_price": price})
        value = min(before["ask"], max(lowest, value))
        self.ask = value
        price = p.price_for(case, terms, value)
        out = [{**terms, "unit_price": price}]
        alt = d.get("alternative") or {}
        if len(alt) == 1 and p.alternatives:
            (k, v), = alt.items()
            options = case["term_options"].get(k) or []
            if k in terms and (v in options or v == p.standard.get(k)) and v != terms[k]:
                s2 = p.nearest_allowed(case, {**terms, k: v})
                if s2 != terms:
                    out.append({**s2, "unit_price": p.price_for(case, s2, value)})
        final = decision == "final_offer" or final_locked or sh.status == "final_offer" or value <= p.full_cost + 1e-6
        if best and ours_value is not None and ours_value >= value - 1e-6 and p.allows(best):
            return self._out("agreed", [dict(best)], text, reasons, claims, attach, agreed=True)
        return self._out("final_offer" if final else "open", out, text, reasons, claims, attach)

    def _out(self, status, sheets, text, reasons, claims, attach, agreed=False):
        """The e-mail with the code's numbers in place of the LLM's placeholders."""
        price = f"€{sheets[0]['unit_price']:.2f}" if sheets else ""
        alt = f"€{sheets[1]['unit_price']:.2f}" if len(sheets) > 1 else price
        body_lines = [text.replace("{PRICE}", price).replace("{ALT_PRICE}", alt)]
        msg = self._mail(status, sheets, [], attach)
        sign = f"\n\n{self.p.sender_name or self.p.name}"
        msg["body"] = body_lines[0].strip() + ("" if (self.p.sender_name or self.p.name) in body_lines[0] else sign)
        msg["claim_results"] = claims
        self.reasons[-1]["lines"] = reasons
        self.reasons[-1]["llm"] = True
        return msg

    def opening(self):
        """Twins keep their real opening e-mail; other suppliers get one written by the LLM."""
        if self.brain is None or self.p.opening_body or self.p.no_bid:
            return super().opening()
        terms = dict(self.p.opening)
        drivers = ""
        if self.package is not None:
            rows = self.package.query(
                f"select series_id, weight from cost_drivers where part_id in ({','.join('?' * len(self.case['parts']))})",
                tuple(self.case["parts"]),
            )
            parts = []
            for r in rows[:3]:
                ids = self.package.ids(f"idx:{r['series_id']}@")
                if len(ids) >= 13:
                    a, b = self.package.lookup(ids[-13])["value"], self.package.lookup(ids[-1])["value"]
                    parts.append(f"{r['series_id']} {(b / a - 1) * 100:+.1f} % in twelve months, {r['weight']:.0%} of cost")
            drivers = "; ".join(parts)
        user = (
            f"Write your quote e-mail for this enquiry (50-120 words). Your offered terms: {_sheet_text(terms)}. "
            f"Write {{PRICE}} where the price goes. Your cost drivers (true figures you may quote): {drivers or 'none given'}. "
            'Reply as JSON: {"email": "...", "reasons": []}'
        )
        try:
            d = self.brain.ask(SYSTEM + "\n\nWHO YOU ARE\n" + self._brief(), user)
            self.llm_calls += 1
            msg = self._mail("open", [terms], [], subject=f"Quote from {self.p.name}: {self.case['title']}")
            msg["body"] = str(d.get("email", "")).replace("{PRICE}", f"€{terms['unit_price']:.2f}")
            return msg
        except Exception as e:
            self.llm_fail += 1
            log.warning("LLM supplier opening failed (%s): template used", e)
            return super().opening()

def _complete_json():
    """An LLM call returning parsed JSON: OpenAI-compatible endpoints with JSON mode, else the kit's."""
    import httpx

    provider = os.environ.get("LLM_PROVIDER", "openai")
    model = os.environ.get("LAB_SUPPLIER_MODEL") or os.environ.get("LLM_MODEL")
    if provider != "openai":

    base = os.environ.get("LLM_BASE_URL", "https://api.openai.com/v1").rstrip("/")

        body = {
            "model": model,
            "messages": [{"role": "system", "content": system}, {"role": "user", "content": user}],
            "response_format": {"type": "json_object"},
        }
        for attempt in range(4):
            r = client.post(f"{base}/chat/completions", json=body, headers=headers)
            if r.status_code == 400 and "response_format" in r.text and "response_format" in body:
                body.pop("response_format")
                continue
            if r.status_code in (429, 500, 502, 503, 504) and attempt < 3:
                time.sleep(float(r.headers.get("retry-after", 2 ** attempt)))
                continue
            r.raise_for_status()
            text = r.json()["choices"][0]["message"]["content"]
            return json.loads(re.search(r"\{.*\}", text, re.S).group(0))
        raise RuntimeError("LLM call failed after retries")

    return call


class Brain:
    """The LLM behind the suppliers of a process, with a disk cache (same prompt, same answer)."""

    def __init__(self, cache=True):
        self.call, self.cache = _complete_json(), cache
        self.calls = self.cached = self.failed = 0

    def ask(self, system, user):
        key = hashlib.sha256((system + "\n" + user).encode()).hexdigest()
        path = CACHE / f"{key}.json"
        if self.cache and path.exists():
            self.cached += 1
            return json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        self.calls += 1
        out = self.call(system, user)
        if self.cache:
            CACHE.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            path.write_text(json.dumps(out), encoding="utf-8")
        return out


def dossier(package, persona, case):
    """What the person knows about its own company and its history with Hollerau, from the data."""
    out, sid = [], persona.supplier_id
    if package is not None:
        intel = package.query("select * from supplier_intel where supplier_id = ?", (sid,))
        if intel:
            i = intel[0]
            out.append(
                f"Company: {persona.name}, {i.get('legal_form') or ''}, founded {i.get('founded')}, owner type "
                f"{i.get('owner_type')}{', group ' + i['group_parent'] if i.get('group_parent') else ''}, "
                f"{i.get('staff')} staff, turnover {i.get('turnover_band')}, equity ratio {i.get('equity_ratio_pct')} %, "
                f"credit index {i.get('credit_index')} (12 months ago {i.get('credit_index_12m_ago')}; higher is worse)."
            )
        hist = package.query(
            "select date, part_id, type, asked_pct, settled_pct, note from negotiation_history where supplier_id = ? "
            "order by date",
            (sid,),
        )
        if hist:
            out.append(
                "Past price rounds with Hollerau: "
                + "; ".join(
                    f"{h['date'][:7]} {h['type']}: asked {h['asked_pct']} %, settled {h['settled_pct']} %"
                    + (f" ({h['note']})" if h.get("note") else "")
                    for h in hist[-6:]
                    if h.get("asked_pct") is not None
                )
            )
        docs = package.query("select id, date, kind, subject from documents where supplier_id = ? order by date", (sid,))
        texts = []
        for d in docs[-8:]:
            try:
                body = package.document(d["id"])
            except (FileNotFoundError, ValueError):
                continue
            body = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", body.split("\n", 3)[-1])[:500]
            texts.append(f"[{d['date']} {d['kind']}: {d['subject']}] {body}")
        if texts:
            out.append("Letters, e-mails and notes about you (some written by the buyer's staff):\n" + "\n".join(texts))
        news = package.query("select date, headline, body from news where supplier_id = ? order by date", (sid,))
        if news:
            out.append("News about you: " + " | ".join(f"{n['date']} {n['headline']}" for n in news[-4:]))
    if persona.notes:
        out.append(f"What we know of your behaviour: {persona.notes}")
    return "\n".join(out)


def profile(persona, case, package):
    """The standing brief for the LLM: who it is and what its business needs."""
    b = case["buyer"]
    lines = [
        f"You are {persona.sender_name or 'the sales manager'} at {persona.name}.",
        ARCHETYPE_TEXT.get(persona.archetype, ""),
        f"Your style of writing: {persona.style} (family: warm, personal; corporate: formal; casual: short, direct).",
        f"The enquiry: {case['title']}. Parts: {', '.join(case['parts'])}. Need about {b['need_per_year']} pieces "
        f"a year. Negotiable: {', '.join(case['negotiable'])}. Fixed: {json.dumps(case.get('fixed_terms', {}))}.",
        f"Your own standard terms: {json.dumps({k: v for k, v in persona.standard.items() if k in NAMES})}.",
    ]
    rate = persona.rate
    if rate >= 0.15:
        lines.append(f"Cash is tight for you (your cost of money is about {rate:.0%} a year): faster payment is worth a lot to you.")
    elif rate <= 0.07:
        lines.append("Money is cheap for you: payment terms matter little to you, price matters.")
    if persona.premiums.get("lead_time_days"):
        lines.append("Your capacity is busy: a shorter lead time than your standard costs you overtime.")
    if persona.premiums.get("fixed_price"):
        lines.append("You carry material price risk: a fixed price without an index clause costs you a premium.")
    if persona.premiums.get("ppm_commitment"):
        lines.append(f"Your real defect rate is about {persona.ppm_real} ppm: a tighter quality commitment costs you money.")
    if persona.hard_limits:
        lines.append(f"Lines you do not cross: {json.dumps(persona.hard_limits)}.")
    lines.append("You are open about costs and may send a cost breakdown if asked." if persona.discloses else
                 "Your costs, margin and calculation stay internal; you do not send cost breakdowns.")  # fmt: skip
    if persona.claim_kinds:
        lines.append(f"Data that tends to convince you when verified: {', '.join(persona.claim_kinds)}.")
    history = dossier(package, persona, case)
    if history:
        lines.append(history)
    return "\n".join(x for x in lines if x)


def _sheet_text(terms):
    return ", ".join(f"{NAMES.get(k, k)} {fmt(k, v)}" for k, v in terms.items())


class LLMSupplierThread(SupplierThread):
    """A supplier thread whose replies an LLM writes and decides, inside the engine's bounds."""

    def __init__(self, persona, case, rng=None, session=None, brain=None, package=None):
        super().__init__(persona, case, rng, session)
        self.brain, self.package = brain, package
        self.brief = None
        self.llm_calls = self.llm_fail = 0

    def _brief(self):
        if self.brief is None:
            self.brief = profile(self.p, self.case, self.package)
        return self.brief

    def _shadow(self):
        """A copy that can run the engine without touching this thread or the session."""
        sh = copy.copy(self)
        sh.messages, sh.reasons, sh.history = list(self.messages), list(self.reasons), list(self.history)
        sh.rng = copy.deepcopy(self.rng)
        if self.session is not None:
            s = copy.copy(self.session)
            s.used, s.offers = set(self.session.used), dict(self.session.offers)
            sh.session = s
        return sh

    def respond(self, msg):
        if self.brain is None:
            return super().respond(msg)
        before = {k: getattr(self, k) for k in ("ask", "status", "round")}
        sh = self._shadow()
        engine = sh.respond(msg)  # the engine's own reply and the state after it
        try:
            out = self._decide(msg, engine, sh, before)
            self.llm_calls += 1
            return out
        except Exception as e:  # the engine's reply stands, and it is counted
            self.llm_fail += 1
            log.warning("LLM supplier failed (%s): the engine's reply is used", e)
            return self._adopt(sh, engine)

    def _adopt(self, sh, engine):
        """Take over the shadow's state and reply as this thread's own."""
        for k in ("ask", "status", "pressure", "mirror", "best_ours", "leaked", "warm", "counters", "timeouts",
                  "approved", "pending", "round", "closed", "standing"):  # fmt: skip
            setattr(self, k, getattr(sh, k))
        if self.session is not None:
            self.session.used |= sh.session.used
        self.history.append(engine)
        self.messages.append(engine)
        self.reasons.append(sh.reasons[-1])
        for ts in engine.get("term_sheets") or []:
            if self.session is not None:
                self.session.offers[ts["term_sheet_id"]] = (self.p.supplier_id, ts["terms"])
        return engine

    def _decide(self, msg, engine, sh, before):
        p, case = self.p, self.case
        sheets = [ts.get("terms", ts) for ts in msg.get("term_sheets") or []]
        best = max(sheets, key=lambda s: p.value(case, s)) if sheets else (self.standing or {}).get("terms")
        structure = {k: v for k, v in (best or {}).items() if k != "unit_price"}
        structure = p.nearest_allowed(case, structure)
        a, e, f = before["ask"], sh.ask, p.full_cost
        verified = [r for r in engine.get("claim_results") or [] if r["result"] == "verified"]
        feats = read(msg.get("body") or "")
        extra = 0.6 * max(0.0, a - e) + (0.1 * max(0.0, a - f) if verified else 0.0)
        if feats["appreciation"] and "family" in p.traits:
            extra += 0.03 * max(0.0, a - f)
        final_locked = before["status"] == "final_offer"
        lowest = a if final_locked else max(f, e - extra)

        def price_at(value, s=structure):
            return p.price_for(case, s, value)

        p_ask, p_engine, p_low = price_at(a), price_at(e), price_at(lowest)
        ours = {**structure, "unit_price": best["unit_price"]} if best and "unit_price" in best else None
        ours_value = p.value(case, best) if best else None
        thread = []
        for m in self.history[-8:]:
            who = "BUYER" if m.get("from") == "buyer" else f"YOU ({m.get('status')})"
            ts = "; ".join(_sheet_text(t.get("terms", t)) for t in m.get("term_sheets") or [])
            thread.append(f"{who}: {re.sub(chr(10) + '+', ' ', (m.get('body') or '')[:700])}" + (f"\n   sheets: {ts}" if ts else ""))
        claims = engine.get("claim_results") or []
        user = "\n".join([
            "THE NEGOTIATION SO FAR (oldest first):", *thread,
            "",
            f"THE BUYER'S NEW E-MAIL (their message {self.round} of {case.get('round_limit', 10)}):",
            msg.get("body") or "(no text)",
            "Their term sheets: " + (" | ".join(_sheet_text(s) for s in sheets) or "none (a question or a holding message)"),
            f"Data they cited, as checked against the records: {[c['result'] for c in claims] or 'none'}",
            "",
            "YOUR NUMBERS FOR THIS REPLY (on the terms of the buyer's best sheet: "
            f"{_sheet_text(structure) or 'its terms'}):",
            f"- your current offer is worth EUR {p_ask:.2f} on these terms",
            f"- LOWEST_ALLOWED this round: EUR {p_low:.2f}" + (" (you are at your final offer)" if final_locked else ""),
            f"- a typical move for you now would be EUR {p_engine:.2f}",
            f"- the buyer offers EUR {best['unit_price']:.2f}" if ours else "- the buyer sent no price",
            f"- your status so far: {before['status']}; your patience: {'running out' if sh.pressure >= p.patience - 1 else 'fine'}",
            "- a bigger move than usual needs your boss's approval" if p.approval_at and not self.approved else "",
            f"- the engine's own decision would be: {engine['status']}",
        ])  # fmt: skip
        d = self.brain.ask(SYSTEM + "\n\nWHO YOU ARE\n" + self._brief(), user)
        return self._apply(d, msg, engine, sh, before, structure, best, ours_value, lowest, final_locked)

    def _apply(self, d, msg, engine, sh, before, structure, best, ours_value, lowest, final_locked):
        p, case = self.p, self.case
        decision = str(d.get("decision", "counter")).lower()
        # the state the engine reached (pressure, mirror, claims used, ...), then our own move on it
        for k in ("pressure", "mirror", "best_ours", "leaked", "warm", "counters", "timeouts", "approved", "pending",
                  "round"):  # fmt: skip
            setattr(self, k, getattr(sh, k))
        if self.session is not None:
            self.session.used |= sh.session.used
        claims = engine.get("claim_results") or []
        attach = []
        for kind in d.get("attach") or []:
            if kind == "cost_breakdown" and p.discloses:
                from .bot import breakdown_text

                price = (self.standing or {}).get("terms", {}).get("unit_price") or p.opening["unit_price"]
                attach.append(("cost-breakdown", breakdown_text(p, price)))
            elif kind == "delivery_schedule":
                from .bot import schedule_text

                attach.append(("delivery-schedule", schedule_text(p, case, self.standing)))
            elif kind == "8d_report":
                from .bot import eight_d_text

                attach.append(("8d-report", eight_d_text(p, case)))
        feats = read(msg.get("body") or "")
        provoked = feats["ultimatum"] or feats["hostile"] or final_locked or self.round >= case.get("round_limit", 10) - 1
        if decision == "walk_away" and not provoked:
            decision = "final_offer" if self.round > 2 else "hold"
        if engine["status"] == "walked_away" and decision not in ("walk_away",):
            decision = "final_offer" if final_locked else decision  # the person may stay, as a final offer
        text = str(d.get("email") or "")
        reasons = [str(r) for r in d.get("reasons") or []][:4]
        if decision == "walk_away":
            self.closed, self.ask = "walked_away", before["ask"]
            return self._out("walked_away", [], text, reasons, claims, attach)
        if decision == "agree" and best and ours_value is not None and ours_value >= lowest - 1e-6 and p.allows(best):
            self.ask = min(before["ask"], max(lowest, ours_value))
            return self._out("agreed", [dict(best)], text, reasons, claims, attach, agreed=True)
        if decision == "hold" or (not msg.get("term_sheets") and decision != "final_offer"):
            self.ask = before["ask"]
            sheets = [self.standing["terms"]] if self.standing else []
            return self._out(before["status"], sheets, text, reasons, claims, attach)
        # counter or final offer: its price on its terms, kept inside the bounds
        terms = dict(structure)
        for k, v in (d.get("terms") or {}).items():
            options = case["term_options"].get(k) or []
            if k in terms and k != "unit_price" and (v in options or v == p.standard.get(k)):
                terms[k] = v
        terms = p.nearest_allowed(case, terms)
        try:
            price = float(d.get("price"))
        except (TypeError, ValueError):
            price = p.price_for(case, terms, sh.ask)
        value = p.value(case, {**terms, "unit_price": price})
        value = min(before["ask"], max(lowest, value))
        self.ask = value
        price = p.price_for(case, terms, value)
        out = [{**terms, "unit_price": price}]
        alt = d.get("alternative") or {}
        if len(alt) == 1 and p.alternatives:
            (k, v), = alt.items()
            options = case["term_options"].get(k) or []
            if k in terms and (v in options or v == p.standard.get(k)) and v != terms[k]:
                s2 = p.nearest_allowed(case, {**terms, k: v})
                if s2 != terms:
                    out.append({**s2, "unit_price": p.price_for(case, s2, value)})
        final = decision == "final_offer" or final_locked or sh.status == "final_offer" or value <= p.full_cost + 1e-6
        if best and ours_value is not None and ours_value >= value - 1e-6 and p.allows(best):
            return self._out("agreed", [dict(best)], text, reasons, claims, attach, agreed=True)
        return self._out("final_offer" if final else "open", out, text, reasons, claims, attach)

    def _out(self, status, sheets, text, reasons, claims, attach, agreed=False):
        """The e-mail with the code's numbers in place of the LLM's placeholders."""
        price = f"€{sheets[0]['unit_price']:.2f}" if sheets else ""
        alt = f"€{sheets[1]['unit_price']:.2f}" if len(sheets) > 1 else price
        body_lines = [text.replace("{PRICE}", price).replace("{ALT_PRICE}", alt)]
        msg = self._mail(status, sheets, [], attach)
        sign = f"\n\n{self.p.sender_name or self.p.name}"
        msg["body"] = body_lines[0].strip() + ("" if (self.p.sender_name or self.p.name) in body_lines[0] else sign)
        msg["claim_results"] = claims
        self.reasons[-1]["lines"] = reasons
        self.reasons[-1]["llm"] = True
        return msg

    def opening(self):
        """Twins keep their real opening e-mail; other suppliers get one written by the LLM."""
        if self.brain is None or self.p.opening_body or self.p.no_bid:
            return super().opening()
        terms = dict(self.p.opening)
        drivers = ""
        if self.package is not None:
            rows = self.package.query(
                f"select series_id, weight from cost_drivers where part_id in ({','.join('?' * len(self.case['parts']))})",
                tuple(self.case["parts"]),
            )
            parts = []
            for r in rows[:3]:
                ids = self.package.ids(f"idx:{r['series_id']}@")
                if len(ids) >= 13:
                    a, b = self.package.lookup(ids[-13])["value"], self.package.lookup(ids[-1])["value"]
                    parts.append(f"{r['series_id']} {(b / a - 1) * 100:+.1f} % in twelve months, {r['weight']:.0%} of cost")
            drivers = "; ".join(parts)
        user = (
            f"Write your quote e-mail for this enquiry (50-120 words). Your offered terms: {_sheet_text(terms)}. "
            f"Write {{PRICE}} where the price goes. Your cost drivers (true figures you may quote): {drivers or 'none given'}. "
            'Reply as JSON: {"email": "...", "reasons": []}'
        )
        try:
            d = self.brain.ask(SYSTEM + "\n\nWHO YOU ARE\n" + self._brief(), user)
            self.llm_calls += 1
            msg = self._mail("open", [terms], [], subject=f"Quote from {self.p.name}: {self.case['title']}")
            msg["body"] = str(d.get("email", "")).replace("{PRICE}", f"€{terms['unit_price']:.2f}")
            return msg
        except Exception as e:
            self.llm_fail += 1
            log.warning("LLM supplier opening failed (%s): template used", e)
            return super().opening()
